noi_dung:
Some Notes About the Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas

(The Sagely City of Ten Thousand Buddhas)

Unlike Buddhism in the East, which has more than 2,000 years of history, Buddhism in America is only in its infancy, sprouting in about this century. Therefore, when bringing the Buddha Dharma to America, the need for the Sangha is to first deeply understand the Buddha teachings, understand the Tripitaka, have high moral conduct, and then be able to apply the Buddha's principles to integrate them with Western culture, using the language of the times. The main foundation in propagating the Dharma is to build a forest, establish a monastic regime with strict precepts, and create favorable conditions for the Sangha and Nuns to study, research, practice and practice the Dharma.

With these key points, in 1959, Venerable Master Hsuan Hua, the disciple who inherited the seal of the Great Venerable Hu Van, founded the Dharma Realm Buddhist Association to proactively propagate the Dharma. In 1966, the Buddhist Lecture Hall at Old Kim Son was established, followed by Kim Son Pagoda.

In 1973, the International Institute of I Ching was born. The main purpose of the Institute is to accurately and understandably translate the Tripitaka (Sutras, Laws, Treatises) from Sanskrit and Chinese into other languages around the world such as English, French, Spanish, Japanese and Vietnamese. Along with the main text, the translation is also accompanied by explanations by Venerable Master Hsuan Hua, so that modern readers can easily understand Buddhist principles and easily apply them to practice and practical life. A special feature of the Institute is that the translation by the Sangha must go through four stages: Translate from the original text, check the meaning of the translation, refine the text and finally certify the translation.

In 1976, the Venerable Master founded the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, a large forest with more than 70 buildings, located on 500 acres of land in Talmage, northern California. All monks, nuns, and lay people, regardless of nationality, can come and practice in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas because the main purpose of Tung Lam is for all sentient beings who sincerely want to practice there. That same year, 1976, the Venerable founded Dharma Realm University with four purposes: Spreading the teachings of Buddhism, molding people's true minds, benefiting society and enlightening all sentient beings.

The monks, nuns, and lay people residing in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas all live frugally, following the Six Principles of the Holy City: Don't fight, Don't be greedy, Don't seek, Don't be selfish, Don't seek personal gain and Don't lie. Young men and women in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas live in isolation; Every day, children can attend Duc Luong Primary School or Virtue Cultivation High School, which is an affiliated part of Dharma Realm University. Here, students all maintain a pure lifestyle: Be a vegetarian, don't drink alcohol, don't smoke, don't gamble, stay away from television, movies and real-life customs.

Up to now, after nearly 30 years of development, the Dharma Realm Buddha Association

The teachings have founded many ashrams everywhere such as:

-Golden Luan Pagoda in Los Angeles, California, USA (1976); -Kim Phong Pagoda in Seattle, Washington, USA;

-Kim Buddha Temple in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada (1983);

- Hoa Nghiem Pagoda in Calgary, Alberta, Canada (1986); -Dharma Buddha Academy in Luc Quy, Taiwan (1989);

And recently, many more monasteries have been established scattered in the state of California such as Dharma Realm Holy City in Sacramento, Buddhist Monastery & Institute of World Religions in Berkeley, Long Beach Holy Temple in California.

tieu_de: Summary of Venerable Master Hsuan Hua
tom_tat: Venerable Master Hsuan Hua's family name is Bach, his real name is An Tu, his nickname is Do Luan. He is from Song Thanh district, Song Giang province in Northeast China, that is, Manchu
noi_dung:
Summary of Venerable Master Hsuan Hua

Venerable Master Hsuan Hua's family name is Bach, his real name is An Tu, his nickname is Do Luan. He is from Songcheng district, Songjiang province in Northeast China, that is, Manchuria.

His father's name was Phu Hai, specializing in farming. Her mother, surnamed Ho, gave birth to a total of eight children, five boys and three girls; and He is the youngest.

Mrs. Ho adopted a vegetarian diet and recited Buddha's name without interruption. One night, the lady had a dream and saw Amitabha Buddha appearing incarnate, radiating light to illuminate the world, shaking heaven and earth. Startled awake, the lady smelled a wonderful scent throughout the room, and then gave birth to Him.

As soon as he was born, he cried continuously for three days and nights without stopping.

It is because of grief for the suffering of this Saha world.

He lives in a very small village with few houses. Therefore, until the age of eleven, he had never seen a dead person. One day, he and his friends in the village went on a field trip. Suddenly he saw a baby, mouth closed, eyes closed, lying bundled up in the straw on the sidelines. He called but the child did not respond. When he touched it, there was no breath. He was extremely confused so he asked his friends. Someone who understands immediately says: "The baby is dead!" But He was extremely surprised, not understanding what death was. Returning home, he immediately asked his mother, who taught: "Every human being, everyone must die. Some people die of old age, some die of illness, and some die of accidents. Regardless of whether one is rich or poor, whether one is a scholar, a farmer, a worker, a merchant, or a mandarin, everyone will eventually die.

He asked again: "If that's true, is there any way to escape death?" At that time, there was a guest in the house who had practiced the Way in the past. He replied: "Only by cultivating the Way, enlightening one's own mind, and fully understanding one's original nature can one end birth and death, transcend samsara, attain Perfect Enlightenment, and attain Infertility."

Although he was still young at that time, he was deeply enlightened by what the guest said, so he decided to leave the home life to practice the Way.

When He discussed leaving the home life with his mother, she taught: "Leaving the home life is a great thing, but it's not an easy thing to do. We need to have good roots, have great vows power, and need to develop great Bodhi mind to be able to achieve the Supreme Path. Now that you have that kind of heart, I wholeheartedly agree, it's really in line with that old dream. Now I am old, my days are short, my brothers and sisters are all independent. Children should stay to take care of their parents; When I'm gone, you leave the home life to practice, it won't be too late."

He obeyed his parents, and then every day he followed his mother bowing to the Buddha. After bowing to the Buddha, he bowed to his parents.

Day by day, as winter fades and spring comes, he respectfully takes care of his parents as if he were Buddha. Soon his reputation for filial piety spread throughout the four directions, at that time everyone called him Bach Hieu Tu (filial son of the Bach family).

When he was 19 years old, his mother passed away; At that time, he said goodbye to his relatives and went to the temple to bow to Venerable Thuong Tri as his teacher and took refuge, officially leaving the home life and taking ordination. After that, he returned to his mother's grave to pay filial piety for three years. During that time, he lived in a small thatched hut, meditating every day, reading the Mahayana sutras and chanting the name Buddha Amitabha. Many times he sat in meditation and then entered Samadhi, continuously for many weeks without leaving meditation.

One night, people in a nearby village were frightened to see his thatched hut burning with red fire. The red fire glowed straight up in the air and the thatched hut was as bright as day. Many people ran to the grave, shouting: "Hieu Tu's house is on fire!" Hundreds of people in the village came together to carry dippers and buckets to fight the fire. However, when they arrived, they only saw a peaceful thatched hut, no fire burning and He was still peaceful and quiet in meditation!

One time he was meditating when suddenly a visitor came to visit. That guest, surprisingly, was the Sixth Patriarch Huineng! The Patriarch taught him that in the future he would go to America to save sentient beings, that in the West he would meet many predestined people who could propagate the Buddha Dharma and that he would save boundless sentient beings. It was not until the Patriarch said goodbye and turned away that he woke up and remembered that Huineng was originally from the Tang Dynasty, 1,200 years ago. After World War II, he traveled everywhere. Finally, after traveling more than three thousand miles, he arrived at Nam Hoa Pagoda and paid homage to the Great Wise One of that time, Elder Venerable Hu Van. The Venerable was 109 years old at that time; As soon as he saw Him, the Venerable immediately recognized His enlightenment. At that time, the Venerable said: "Like thi, like thi!"; and He also replied: "Like thi, like thi!"

At that time, Old Venerable Hu Van confirmed his attainment, and he officially became the ninth Patriarch of the Quy Ngoc dharma lineage.

After that, the Venerable Master taught him to stay at the temple and take on the position of Head of the Precepts Institute of Nam Hoa Temple.

In 1950, he left the temple and left for Hong Kong. Here, He lives in an isolated cave, without visiting dust or worldly things. Soon, countless monks from Mainland China came to Hong Kong as refugees, and they needed His help. Finally, according to fate, he left the cave, established a lecture hall and two pagodas, and helped build many other ashrams.

During his twelve years in Hong Kong, he was a shining example of asceticism, diligence in cultivating the Way, and forgetting himself for the sake of Buddha Dharma. He influenced countless good men and women, causing them to develop the Bodhi mind, take refuge in the Three Jewels, and support the Buddha Dharma.

In 1962, he came to San Francisco, USA. Here, in a small warehouse, he persistently practiced in silence, waiting for the opportunity to propagate the Dharma to ripen. At that time, he called himself "The Middle Monk's Tomb". (the monk in the grave), or Hoat Tu Nhan (the person who died but is still alive). Buddhists who understand His true practice are very moved and respectfully support and make offerings to Him.

In 1968, he knew the opportunity had come; He said: "A flower will bloom with five petals." That summer, he presided over a Dharma conference teaching the Shurangama Sutra for 96 days. When the Dharma Conference ended, sure enough, the first five Americans asked to become monks with him.

From then on, he continued to preside over many other Dharma conferences, explaining the Mind

Sutra, Ksitigarbha Sutra, Lotus Sutra, Dharma Jewel Platform Sutra, etc.

In 1971, he preached the supreme sutra of Mahayana, which is the Avatamsaka Sutra.

Along with preaching the Sutras and preaching the Dharma, he also performed countless other merits of saving sentient beings. In 1976, he established the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, a base to propagate Buddha Dharma in the United States. In the Holy City, he built the Tung Lam regime, trained monks and nuns, studied them, and created excellent conditions for true practice.

Venerable Master Hsuan Hua's Eighteen Great Vows

When Venerable Master Hsuan Hua was 19 years old, his mother passed away. After taking care of the burial, he went to Tam Duyen Pagoda

Harbin, officially leaving the home life, bows to the Venerable Master

Thuong Tri is the Teacher. Not long after, he came to the grave of his filial mother. That year, on the day of Lord Avalokitesvara's death, June 19, before all Buddhas, Bodhisattva made eighteen great vows:

"Respectful Buddha of the ten directions,

Along with the Dharma Tripitaka,

Past and present, Sage Monks,

May I invite you to witness:

Disciple Do Luan,

Thich An Tu,

I now have a mind that:

Do not ask for blessings from God, Man,

With Sravaka, Pratyekabuddha,

until the Bodhisattva line of succession.

Only the Supreme Vehicle

but develop Bodhi mind.

May the sentient beings of the Dharma Realm,

Instantly agreed

Nau Da La Tam Mieu Tam Bodhi."

I vow that if there is a Bodhisattva in the ten directions and three lifetimes, in the uttermost emptiness, throughout the Dharma Realm, and has not yet become a Buddha, then I swear that I will not attain Perfect Enlightenment.

I vow that if there is a Pratyekabuddha in the ten directions and three lifetimes, in the uttermost emptiness, throughout the Dharma Realm, who has not yet become a Buddha, I swear that I will not attain Perfect Enlightenment.

I vow that if there is a Sravaka in the ten directions and three lifetimes, in the uttermost emptiness, throughout the Dharma Realm, and has not yet become a Buddha, then I swear that I will not attain perfect Enlightenment.

I vow that if there is a God or a human being in the Three Realms who has not yet become a Buddha, I swear that I will not attain perfect Enlightenment.

I vow that if there is a person in the world of the ten directions who has not yet attained Buddhahood, I vow not to attain perfect Enlightenment.

I vow that if there is a God, Human, or Asura who has not yet attained Buddhahood, I vow not to attain Perfect Enlightenment.

I vow that in the world of animals, if there is any species that has not yet become a Buddha, I vow not to attain perfect Enlightenment.

I vow that in the world of Hungry Ghosts, if there is even one person who has not yet attained Buddhahood, I vow not to attain Perfect Enlightenment.

I vow that in the world of Hell, if there is still one person who has not yet attained Buddhahood, I vow not to attain perfect Enlightenment.

I vow that in the Three Realms, if those who have taken refuge with me, be they Gods, Humans, Asuras, flying or diving creatures, animals, plants, spirits, dragons, animals, demons, or gods, have not yet attained Buddhahood, I swear not to attain perfect Enlightenment.

May all the blissful blessings I deserve be dedicating merit to all sentient beings in the Dharma Realm.

May I alone bear all the sufferings of sentient beings in the Dharma Realm.

I pray that I will divide countless spirits, penetrate the minds of sentient beings who do not believe in the Buddha Dharma, make them abandon evil, turn to goodness, repent and reform themselves, take refuge in the Three Jewels, and finally become Buddha.

I pray that all sentient beings, when they see my face or even hear my name, will develop the mind of Bodhi and quickly attain Buddhahood.

I vow to always respect what the Buddha taught, and practice eating one meal a day.

May the enlightenment of all sentient beings, all sentient beings be absorbed by all sentient beings

muscle.

I pray that in this life I will attain the Five Eyes, Six Insights, and fly freely.

May all prayers be fulfilled.

Finally:

"All sentient beings vow to be saved.

Endless afflictions vows to end.

There are countless teachings to learn.

Buddha's Supreme Way vows to be achieved."

The Eight Rules of the Institute of Classical Translation

Translators must free themselves from the motive of pursuing fame and profit.

Translators must cultivate their minds and cultivate their nature and get rid of the habit of arrogance.

Translators must control themselves and not praise themselves and then criticize others.

Translators must not consider themselves the standard, the measure, and then degrade others by finding mistakes in their work.

The translator must take Buddha's mind as his own mind.

The translator must use Trach Phap Nhan to judge what is true

reason.

The translator must respectfully request the High Monks and Venerables in the ten directions to prove his translation.

The translator must happily spread the Buddha's teachings by printing the Sutras, Rules, and Treatises once his translation is proven to be correct.

"If you plant the cause of Buddha, you will reap the fruit of Buddha. If you plant the cause of Bodhisattva, you will reap the fruit of Bodhisattva."

1. SOW CAPACITY AND RECEIVE FRUITS

"Liu perceives the different species and races of living beings, All perceives, Distinguishes actions.

Try to observe all wisdom, Children are indestructible, but all dharma-natures."

Translated as:

"Knowing the many types of living beings,

It is due to Thought, Action, and discrimination.

Because of observation, one should understand clearly

But it does not destroy the nature of all dharmas."

Because of origin, living beings create karma, receive retribution, and whatever cause they plant, they will reap the result. That is a very natural principle. If you plant the cause of Buddha, you will reap the fruit of Buddha, if you plant the cause of Bodhisattva, you will reap the fruit of Bodhisattva, if you plant the cause of Pratyekabuddha, you will reap the fruit of Pratyekabuddha, if you plant the cause of Sravaka, you will reap the fruit of Sravaka. Buddha, Bodhisattva, Sravaka, Pratyekabuddha are the four Noble Paths.

Among the six mortal paths, there are three good paths: Heaven, Humanity, and Asura; The three evil paths are Animals, Hungry Ghosts, and Hell. In short, if you plant the causes of the three good paths, you will reap the results of the three good paths; if you plant the causes of the three evil paths, you will reap the results of the three evil paths. That principle is correct, not one bit wrong and never changes; and there is absolutely no superstitious nuance at all.

Ignorant people do not know the benefits of cause and effect, so they continue to act arbitrarily, do not believe in cause and effect, and even reject it. People with wisdom know that cause and effect are extremely harmful, so they are afraid of doing things wrong with cause and effect. No matter what you do, you have to think three times before practicing.

The saints in this world practice to end the cycle of cause and effect. Ordinary people create more sins in the cause and effect chain. If there is no crime, more crime will be created; After committing a crime, one refuses to accept it as a crime, but takes it for granted, without the slightest shame. What a piling up of sins that cannot be forgiven!

There are many different types of living beings; In general, there are only two types: good and evil, but each is different. Each type, each thing creates its own karma, then receives its own retributions; But in general, all living beings are in the Five Aggregates (form, feeling, perception, action, consciousness) to form their own distinct karma. If we observe and understand this different karma of retribution, we will understand all dharma natures without destroying the morality of that dharma nature:

"The wise know all Buddhas Dharma,

Di like Thi Hanh Nhi dedicating merit,

Who cares for all sentient beings,

Linh is truly Dharma-minded."

Translated as:

"The wise understand all Buddha Dharma,

So practice to determine merit,

With compassion for all living beings,

Make them think in the right place."

Those who are wise understand the Buddha's Dharma, so they practice Bodhisattva, dedicating the merit of all the good roots they have accumulated. Why does dedicating merit and good roots to sentient beings? Because they care about all living beings! Bodhisattva saw that living beings were too confused; What sentient beings do is crazy. No matter how we teach and transform living beings, they still cannot understand. If you teach them to forget themselves for others, leave the roots behind, support the Dharma, and make the Dharma stand in the world, they will never believe. Living beings are truly pitiful. Therefore, they advise living beings not to do evil things, but to do good things; For true Dharma, you must follow it correctly.

What is not right? Please reflect and think carefully, not just once but often, to see if you have made cause and effect mistakes? Let's see if you have conscientiously fulfilled your responsibilities and obligations with regard to Buddhism, or have you created all kinds of karma and mistakes?

Therefore, everywhere, every time, you must reflect, reflect and reflect, examine and examine, then you will truly be a true follower of Buddhism!

tieu_de: 2. REFLECTIONS COMPLETELY
tom_tat: Buddhism often says "return to originality," meaning that whatever we were in the past will return to being like that; But what was my future like in the past? In the past, there was nothing. So now to revert means to return...
noi_dung:
2. REFLECTIONS COMPLETELY

(Van Buddha Thanh March 10, 1977)

Buddhism often says "return to originality," That means whatever we were like in the past will be like that again; But what was my future like in the past? In the past, there was nothing. So now to revert means to return to a state where nothing exists.

Whenever we have a little attachment, there is an obstacle. If there are obstacles, you cannot leave the Three Realms, so you must destroy all attachments. When I get to the place where there is nothing, that's when I restore my true face. Right now I can't have anything even if I want it. Wait until I don't want anything then I'll have everything. Wisdom will appear, magical powers will appear, wonderful uses will appear.

Why don't I have wisdom or supernatural powers? It's because I go from place to place collecting trash, and I don't want the gold, silver, and jewels. I don't want my own precious existence, so I throw it away, I just look for trash and consider myself very smart. Actually, it's really so delusional!

USE A NORMAL MIND TO LEARN Buddha

"Lo Dao Tri Horsepower,

The Japanese see the human heart."

Translated as:

"Traveling long distances, knowing the strength of horses. After many days and months, knowing people's hearts."

Those who study the Way cannot learn the Buddha Dharma in just one day or one night. It takes a long time to experience the teachings of the Buddha. Only by following that teaching can one achieve success.

A person who truly realizes the Buddha Dharma is neither frightened nor afraid, neither happy nor sad. Buddha Dharma is like this: There's nothing to worry about, nothing to be happy or sad about. Must always maintain the state of "as if motionless, ever-clear" (1) because that is the nature of Buddha Dharma!

tieu_de: 4. STUDYING Buddha, DON'T BE greedy for fame and profit
tom_tat: People who study Buddha Dharma need to always practice diligently with sincerity, like two feet standing firmly on the ground (tread on the ground), and not make false plans.
noi_dung:
4. STUDYING Buddha, DON'T BE greedy for fame and profit

(Van Buddha Thanh March 15, 1977)

People who study Buddha Dharma should always practice diligently with sincerity, like standing firmly on the ground with both feet (treading the ground), not scheming for vanity.

Loving vain fame is of no benefit to cultivating the Way. Wanting to do "real and anonymous" things Do not be greedy for "nothing but real things"; That means not being greedy for a false name, having a reputation but not having any money. As for doing things that are truly manifest on the outside, they are called "anonymous real things"!

You should not be greedy for vain names; Every action, every word, every thought must be true. Honest heart, honest work, is the identity of Buddhist followers. If your mind is full of morality, education and wisdom, then you can call yourself capable!

Don't be greedy for vain fame, don't like worldly gain; otherwise it's just like "fake flower petals" can never bear "fruit" really okay. That is a very important point, please pay attention!

tieu_de: NOTES ON THE SPIRITUALITY OF PRAYING FOR RAIN AT GOLDEN GATE PARK - SAN FRANCISCO
tom_tat: San Francisco and surrounding areas hundreds of miles away were in drought. For two consecutive years, there has been very little rain, not only making it difficult to grow crops, but drinking water has also become a serious problem, so using water every day...
noi_dung:
NOTES ON THE SPIRITUALITY OF PRAYING FOR RAIN AT GOLDEN GATE PARK - SAN FRANCISCO

(Narrated by an insider)

San Francisco and surrounding areas hundreds of miles away were in drought. For two consecutive years, there was very little rain, not only making it difficult to grow crops, but drinking water also became a serious problem, so daily water use was limited. Therefore, those who leave the home life and lay at Kim Son temple automatically develop the mind to pray for rain and practice Bodhisattva.

At seven o'clock in the morning on December 16, 1977, at Golden Gate Park, Master Heng Thuc set up an altar to pray for rain. A total of several hundred people participated sincerely chanting mantras to pray for rain. The Dharma Conference is extremely solemn; From the time America was founded until now, this is the first Dharma conference. People who are not followers of Buddhism think it's superstitious and it can't happen. At the end of the Dharma Conference, everyone left with the firm belief that rain would come. The ancients have a saying:

"Star becomes the will, Gold and stone are open."

Meaning:

"The utmost sincerity, even gold and stone melt."

So, the next day at around twelve o'clock in the afternoon, the sky was clear and transparent, suddenly dark clouds gathered, thunder and lightning appeared, and in an instant the rain fell everywhere. Everyone was extremely happy.

The sudden rain surprised meteorological experts. This phenomenon is due to the "induction of communication": The great sincerity of those who prayed for rain influenced the compassion of the Dragon King, so even though it was not the time for it to rain, the rain still poured down to save sentient beings!

The drought was eliminated after that rain. This news spread throughout San Francisco, journalists and television stations came to interview, take pictures, and film. This story was spread as extremely strange. The writer who participated in this Dharma Conference to pray for rain should write it down for readers to know.

tieu_de: 6. RECRUITMENT OF QUALIFIED CANDIDATES TO BE ABROAD
tom_tat: In the future, Kim Luan, Kim Son and Tathagata pagodas all need an Abbot. Therefore, you should nominate a talented and virtuous person who is qualified to be the Abbot, and then support him.
noi_dung:
6. RECRUITMENT OF QUALIFIED CANDIDATES TO BE ABROAD

(Van Buddha Thanh January 16, 1978)

In the future, Kim Luan, Kim Son and Tathagata pagodas all need an Abbot. Therefore, you should nominate a talented and virtuous person who is qualified to be the Abbot, and then support that person.

When choosing an Abbot, what should be the criteria? Firstly, that person must not be angry, must behave in a peaceful manner, and can create predestined relationships with living beings everywhere; Do not use power to overwhelm others, know how to use democratic style to work so that everyone respects you.

If you choose an Abbot who is prone to anger, no one will be able to withstand his oppression, everyone will be dissatisfied, and peace will no longer exist. This will not help Buddhism at all, but on the contrary, it will cause difficulties!

Anyone who can eliminate anger and know how to be extremely patient will of course be elected Abbot; If otherwise, I'm afraid there is little hope. Why? Because afflictions are very easy to remove

Buddha's teachings are destroyed! Affliction belongs to the fire that can destroy everything, even if there is a heavy rain like just mentioned, it cannot extinguish this great disaster.

Today, January 16, 1978, I tell you these important words because in the future when selecting an Abbot, you need to consider his virtue and knowledge. Anyone who is an Abbot must have a generous and good relationship, be in harmony with everyone, work together, be respected by everyone, and not make anyone resentful or hateful.

Regardless of whether they are Bhikkhus, Bhiksunis, Upasakas, Upasayas, if you see someone who has the Dharma mind, is diligent in practice, has leadership ability, and is worthy of being an Abbot, then that person can be nominated to be an Abbot!

tieu_de: The Lankavatara Sutra is ABSOLUTELY THE COMPONENT SUTRA
tom_tat: Today is December 17, 1976 (Amitabha's astral day), I face all Buddhas making vows in front of the ten directions as follows. What wish? This vow is related to the issue of the Shurangama Sutra which is really interesting
noi_dung:
The Lankavatara Sutra is ABSOLUTELY THE COMPONENT SUTRA

Today is December 17, 1976 (Amitabha's astral day), I face all Buddhas making vows in front of the ten directions as follows. What wish? This vow is related to the issue of whether the Shurangama Sutra is real or fake.

Recently, many scholars have criticized the Shurangama Sutra, claiming that this Sutra was not spoken by Shakyamuni Buddha himself, but was fabricated by later generations. That is destructive propaganda, causing many believers to not want to deeply understand the Buddha's Dharma and to be slanderous and skeptical. Many people listen to it and follow it, but they don't know what a prosthetic is like, which is very pitiful!

Today, I assure everyone that the Shurangama Sutra is the true sutra; Not only the Shurangama Sutra but also the Shurangama Mantra are also true! The Shurangama Sutra is Buddha's true body, Buddha's relics, no one can destroy it!

Without the Shurangama Sutra, there is Dharma; without the Shurangama Sutra, there is no Dharma! If the Shurangama Sutra is fake, I vow to have my tongue cut out and fall into the Infinite Hell.

I hope that from now on, you must have Trach Phap Nhan, do not listen to the words of doctors or scholars who study the Shurangama Sutra and think that this Sutra is a fabrication! Don't let yourself be shaken, on the contrary, you need to have Concentration to transform that mistake! Why do those people think that the Shurangama Sutra is fake? It's because they have been deluded to the extreme, don't want the Dharma to stay in the world, don't want others to practice, so they intentionally sabotage it! In the Shurangama Sutra, it is taught that:

"Delusion cannot be eliminated, Tran cannot leave."

Meaning:

"The lust does not end, there is no escape from this world."

Just these two sentences alone are enough to prove that this Sutra contains the true, wonderful truths said by all Buddhas: "If you cannot get rid of lust, you cannot leave the Three Realms. "(2) It can also be said that: If you don't cut off desires and get rid of cravings, it's basically impossible to attain fruition! In the Shurangama Sutra, it is also taught that:

"Weakness does not stop lust,

Practicing meditation,

Like sandstone distillation,

Desire becomes sanskrit,

The land of non-existence."

Meaning:

"Do not stop lusting,

But practice meditation and concentration,

Just like cooking sand,

Then hope becomes rice,

It's impossible."

Therefore, if you contemplate, you will know that the Dharma Eye Treasury is here! All true Buddhists must definitely support and study the Shurangama Sutra and recite the Shurangama mantras, because this Mantra has inconceivable power; that is my own experience.

I again make special vows to emphasize that the Shurangama Sutra is real and not fake. If I make a mistake, I will fall into hell and have my tongue cut out!

I hope you all clearly understand this issue, you must have the right view for yourself, don't disappoint me.

tieu_de: SENTIMENTS ARE SERIOUS WITH THE karma of WONDERFUL VIEW, AND THE SAME DESTINY OF WONDERFUL VIEW.
tom_tat: In the Shurangama Sutra, there is a passage that discusses two types of crazy false views. What are the two crazy things?
noi_dung:
SENTIMENTS ARE SERIOUS WITH THE karma of WONDERFUL VIEW, AND THE SAME DESTINY OF WONDERFUL VIEW.

In the Shurangama Sutra, there is a passage that discusses two types of crazy false views. What are the two types of crazy and false views?

The first is called Sentient Beings with False Views of Karma, that is, because we alone create karma that is not the same as everyone else, we interpret our own behavior differently from others, in every case we are completely different. For example, thinking we are the best, harming others for our own benefit, liking far-fetched and illusory things or doing things that no one else dares to do. That is creating karma, and when you create it yourself, you receive it, which is not the same as that of others.

The second type is called the False View of Sentient Beings, that is, created by sentient beings combined with karma, we and all others are the same; Like natural disasters that kill thousands of people, that is called collective karma, which means a number of people suffer together. Those people commit the same evil deeds, so they receive the same retribution.

The word "ant" Here it means understanding, because taking the ignorance of living beings as one's own, accepting the thief as one's child, gives birth to all kinds of attachments and delusions. Due to delusion, delusion is born, due to delusion, countless evil karmas are created, so they receive evil results together.

Now I would like to tell a true story about Communist Karma as follows: In the 33rd year of the Republic of China (1944), in Henan province, China, there was absolutely no rain for a whole year, the land was dry and there was also an epidemic of locusts. Every time these grasshoppers fly, they fill the sky. All agricultural products were eaten by them, not even a blade of grass or a leaf could grow. At that time, a child saw in the sky an old man carrying a bag, from morning to afternoon, always throwing down grasshoppers from that bag flying all over the sky. The people there were so hungry that they spread nets to catch grasshoppers to eat to alleviate their hunger. They think that grasshoppers are also an agricultural product so they are not poisonous. Who would have thought that when these grasshoppers were cooked, they would turn into feces and mud, inedible, and no one would dare to eat them. Because they were so hungry, the people had no choice but to move to another place. From Henan province to Chang'an is eight hundred miles away, and countless people have died along the way; These people died horribly, everyone who saw them was terrified. This can be said to be an example of "plus karma". But the trick is to get retribution.

Now let's talk about the Special Karma Vong Kien and the Same Fate Vong Kien. In the Shurangama Sutra, Buddha has a very clear explanation. What is Void View Karma? Just like in this world, there are people with dirty eyes who see red in front of their eyes. At night, when they look at lights, they see rings of colorful light surrounding the lights. Because the eyes are sick, they see such illusions, seeing all five mixed colors. This sick eye symbolizes ignorance, at night symbolizes ignorance, the light symbolizes the visceral nature, that is, our original nature, the five colors symbolize the Five Aggregates or Five Aggregates, which are false worlds.

Because sentient beings have false views, there are illusions in the external environment; If false views are eliminated, the illness will no longer exist. How can that illusory light come about? The good eye symbolizes true wisdom, and the light bulb symbolizes truth. If you use true wisdom to see the truth, then the One True Dharma Realm has absolutely no Five Skandhas or Five Objects at all.

Just like there are people whose eyes are not inherently sick, but they themselves cause the disease. Like a guy smoking opium, he once laughed loudly while he was standing in front of a wall.

-I asked: "Why are you laughing?"

-He replied: "It's so strange! This wall is so beautiful, it has all five colors of light shining on all four sides."

That's just an illusion. If you don't have a disease, if you smoke opium, your mind becomes crazy. Those illusions, which were originally false, were thought to be real, so the body was in delusion without knowing that it was delusion! Above is an abridged explanation of the Vong Kien Karma Vajrayana.

Next, the Sutra explains what the Same Fate Vong Kien is. For example, in Jambudvipa there is a small continent with only two countries whose retributions are not the same. The people of a country feel bad fate and encounter unexpected disasters; People in neighboring countries are not affected at all. That is caused by delusion, false karma, false views.

As is currently the case in the United States, the East often has storms and floods that kill many people, but the Southwest is completely unscathed. That's because karma is felt only in the East, not in the Southwest. Or someone sees two suns or two moons, which are both bad signs; the ancients said: "The sky has two days, the people have no two armies." (On, there are no two suns; In a country, there are no two kings.)

In China, during the Xia Dynasty, King Kiet was a tyrant. Suddenly two suns appeared in the air, and the Xia dynasty perished. That is a fierce omen foretold. There are also omens called Vung, Thich, Boi, and Quyet. The evil energy that surrounds the moon and darkens the moon is called Vocabulary; The black gas that covers the moon is called Thich; The white gas next to the moon is called Boi, but half of it is called Quyet. Those are bad omens belonging to the moon.

Chinese history records that when the moon was obscured seven times, Han Cao To in Pengcheng was besieged by the Huns. The star with a long tail of light is called Tue, which means comet; The shorter halo that sweeps in all four directions is called Star Powder; Flying down in the air is called Phi Tinh; If it shoots up from below it is called Luu Tinh; Those are all bad omens belonging to the stars.

In the book Spring and Autumn, it is written that King Song Nhuong Cong was not benevolent, so stars fell like rain. When King Qin Shi Huang was extremely tyrannical, comets appeared; Those are also bad omens. Evil energy above the sun is called Phu, and next to the sun is called Nhi. After it rains, a rainbow appears, it is called Hong Nghe, in the morning it is called Hong, in the afternoon it is called Nghe; Those are all bad omens of the sun. In short, besides the sun and the moon, those gases appear that are all signs of danger.

In China, every time a dynasty changes, unexpected omens occur. Once, an Emperor saw an unusual omen in a star and immediately summoned the Thien Van mandarin to ask if it would be a good or bad omen.

-The Kham Thien Giam said: "This is a very unusual omen. Your Majesty may die, but I have a way to make the Prime Minister suffer that cruel thing on Your Majesty's behalf. Is Your Majesty willing?"

-The king replied: "The Prime Minister takes care of the country's great affairs, so how can he die for me?"

-The official asked: "Is it possible to transfer disaster to the people?"

-"The people are the foundation of the country, I work for the people, how can I let the people die for me?"

-"If so, can this disaster be transferred to the crops?"

-"If crops are lost, people will starve to death, that's something we cannot do!"

After hearing this, Quan Kham Thien Giam immediately prostrated himself and said: "Your Majesty is truly a wise and merciful ruler, he will definitely turn evil things into good things; The Emperor definitely cannot die!"

Sure enough, the next day the bad omen in the sky disappeared and was never seen again. That proves that nothing is fixed, it's just your mind that changes. If the mind is good, it can turn bad things into good things; So Lao Tzu said:

"Return to kindness,

Even though goodness is still a child, goodness depends on the spirit.

Turning my mind towards evil,

Even though evil is still the child of the Evil God."

Translated as:

"Turn your mind towards goodness,

Although the good deed has not yet been done, the Good Spirit has followed closely. Turn your mind to evil,

Although the evil has not yet been done, the evil spirit is already close by."

Gods have good and evil; Good gods protect good people, Evil gods punish evil people, so it is said: "Drawings, blessings are beyond measure, Duy Nhan summons himself." (Damages and blessings have no entrance. They are only brought on by themselves.)If we do not do evil in our hearts, then undesirable (ungood) things cannot arise.

9. reciting mantras FIRST MUST BE CONFIDENTIAL INTENTION

(Van Buddha Thanh January 25, 1981)

"Reciting, remaining silent, saying little,

The teachings bring joy to the great world.

The work of all dharmas leads to salvation,

Nirvana without increase or decrease."

Translated as:

"Recite, recite silently, speak little,

Teaching, benefiting, everywhere.

Everything done is for salvation,

No increase, no decrease, to Nirvana."

To study the Mantra, you first need to have the right mind and sincere intention; If the mind is not right, then whatever mantra you learn will become evil. Only by studying the Mantra will you be inspired. The right mind is not enough, you need to be sincere. "Wall" That is, I am always very attentive, focused, not distracted, and do not do careless or irresponsible things. Only then will there be induction.

If you don't have "right heart and sincere intention," If your heart is full of wrong thoughts and harms others, then you are doing the devil's work. The demon king's Dharma is harmful to others, not beneficial to anyone.

If you really want to practice, under no circumstances should you harm others. We must cultivate the mind to benefit sentient beings; Do not learn Mantras to subdue demons or fight with others.

Buddhist followers have no enemies and do not seek revenge. Regarding those who intentionally harm us, we must be patient and practice the Paramita of Patience; do not have a mind for revenge. That is the sublime, the advantage of Buddhism that other religions lack.

Although Christianity says "love your enemy" (loving the enemy), but that is only in terms of language, can they really show it in action? They always view Buddhists as enemies. Do they love Buddhists? Certainly not, because they call Buddhists perverts and demons!

The most important principle of Buddhism is: If you are a devil, I absolutely will not harm you, will not harbor any resistance, but on the contrary, will find a way to accept you. This is the most special teaching of Buddhism. Always develop compassion for living beings, do not harm others.

The Shurangama Mantra is an earth-shattering mantra that makes ghosts and gods tremble in fear, and is a very effective spiritual text. After learning the Shurangama Mantra, you must always develop a compassionate mind, and use your thoughts not to harm others. If someone is not good to you, don't be upset or resentful. Your mind needs to be as large as three thousand worlds, all things can be contained in your mind; That is the identity of Buddhists!

"Recite, be silent, keep your thoughts to a minimum." The mantra "Yin two na" (Nhan Da La) translated means reciting, or silent thoughts, or minimal thoughts; That is, we don't need to talk much, nor do we have many false thoughts. If we concentrate, we will be spiritual, if we are distracted, we will not be inspired.

What is the most specialized? That is, always do not have the mind to harm sentient beings. If you have the mind to harm others, your future will be extremely dangerous; because: "Multiple acts of dishonesty inevitably cause harm." (If you always do unjust things, you will destroy yourself.)

When we harm others, we harm ourselves. If you kill someone else's father, someone will definitely kill your father; If you kill your brother, someone will kill your brother; That is the law of cause and effect. As Buddhists, we need to do good and avoid evil. If you do not create evil causes, you will avoid evil consequences in the future.

"The teachings bring joy to the great world." This sentence says that using the Buddha Dharma to guide and educate sentient beings, making everyone achieve benefits and joy. When I see something beneficial for others, I do it immediately:

"Fortune builds the mind on earth,

Cultivate the middle nature."

Translated as:

"Cultivate the spiritual soil,

Cultivate the sky of nature."

Often helping others will naturally lead to virtue over time. It's not just calling others to benefit yourself, but not benefiting others yourself. A person who cultivates dependence and only wants to enjoy comfort is a person without courage.

Look at this world, those who seek comfort for themselves end up failing; If you don't believe it, please research carefully. No matter who it is, with bottomless greed and dedicated to finding comfort for themselves, the results will not be good. If we bring benefits to others and make everyone happy, then everyone will respect us wherever we go.

Confucius said: "Speak is loyal, actions are respectful, even though the barbarian branch is ganging, act well." (If your words are truthful, your actions are sincere and respectful, even in dangerous places you will still be safe.)

A word spoken must be truthful and must not be deceitful or deceitful to others. Behavior must be extremely honest, loyal, humble, and respectful. Whatever you do, do it with "humbleness and integrity"; Don't be arrogant, consider yourself like a god, no one can compare to you. This is unacceptable!

tieu_de: DECLARING THE SUCCESS OF THE Shurangama Mantra of Radiant Light on the Buddha's Palace
tom_tat: "The Golden Self returns to the Great Buddhahood, the endless Dharma Treasury of wisdom and light. I pray for the enlightened and marvelous Tathagata to serve the teachings of the Tathagata
noi_dung:
DECLARING THE SUCCESS OF THE Shurangama Mantra of Radiant Light on the Buddha's Palace

"The Golden Self returns to the Great Buddhahood, the endless Dharma Treasury of wisdom and light. I pray to the enlightened willow and wonderful Tathagata, to serve the teachings of the Tathagata."

"The Golden Self Returns to the Great Buddha's Birth": Those are the words of the Dharma Protectors, that they take refuge in the Great Buddha's Shurangama mantra.

"Endless Dharma Treasury of Wisdom Light": The Great Buddha Name is the Buddha's crown and is an endless treasury of Dharma treasures. If you have access to that treasury of Dharma treasures, you will never run out of them. This endless collection of Dharma appears in our own nature, not from the outside. But why doesn't it appear now? The Dharma Treasury is like insects that sleep in the winter, waiting for the warm sunshine of spring to begin to become active again. When the practitioner's body heats up, the self-natured insect will revive, and at the same time all other types of bacteria will die (this bacteria means afflictions).

Is that not killing? If you think this is killing, then you may not need to practice! No one forces you; You can return to the world, you can act like a lay person, full of afflictions, obstacles, struggles, ignorance, and jealousy. But if you want to practice, you must transform those bacteria and restore your Buddha nature.

When I have not yet become a Buddha, I have up to 84,000 types of insects in my body that eat my flesh, drink my blood, and reside in my body. They urged me not to keep my reservations and forced me to do crazy things. Because I was influenced by them, I did all kinds of bad things. If I say: "Oh! That's what they did, not me." So let's ask why do I help them? That means you can't stand being a little hungry, you can't stand being a little thirsty, you can't stand not having enough sleep; Why do I have to help those germs? Helping them will not reveal your true nature!

So what exactly are those germs? That is, being ignorant makes your body uncomfortable here and uncomfortable there; The whole body is so troublesome! Sometimes they make us sick, sometimes they make us sick. These stupid germs make it impossible for us to have enough clothes to wear, not enough food to eat, and in the end we have to struggle with ourselves.

The endless Dharma Treasury arises from the Great Buddhahood. This light of wisdom is not like other lights but is the light of Buddha. Why does Buddha have aura? Because Buddha did not want to have dark, ignorant germs, he used wisdom to illuminate everything, sweeping away ignorance. When ignorance is swept away, the Dharma nature naturally appears, therefore the Light of Wisdom is Buddha light!

"Praying for the enlightenment of the wonderful General Tri" : Why do we pay homage to the Great Buddha Honoring Wisdom Light? Why should we worship the Great Buddha Dharma Wisdom Light? Because I want to understand the Great Patriarch Mantra, also the Dharani Shurangama. The Great Compassion Mantra is also called the Great Compassion Da La Ni.

Da La Ni is Sanskrit Dharani, translated as General Tri. "Total" means to cover all dharmas, "maintain" which means preserving immeasurable meaning. All dharmas are summed up in this mantra, all dharmas originate from this mantra.

Please look at the flag of the Dharma Realm Buddha Association, each pink color on the flag represents the Light of Wisdom. This light from the place of "one" which comes out, so it is said:

"The one nature disperses all enemies,

All enemies return to one origin."

Meaning:

The word "one" but divided into ten thousand things, From ten thousand things return to "one."

Light radiates from one point to ten thousand directions and then from ten thousand directions to one point. Therefore, at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas there is not just "one" but all the auras of all Buddhas are emitted from here, and then that light returns as "one". without violating or obstructing other auras.

"Serve the Tathagata's teachings": Once you understand the meaning of this mantra, you must follow its principles and respectfully practice it.

tieu_de: 11. teaching ON DAY paying homage to the Buddha DAN
tom_tat: Shakyamuni Buddha in the past said: Three stages of cultivating blessings of wisdom, Hundreds of kalpas of good generals. That is, in three Asanga kalpas he cultivated blessings and wisdom, and for hundreds of kalpas he cultivated good appearances. He practiced asceticism, doing things...
noi_dung:
11. teaching ON DAY paying homage to the Buddha DAN

(Van Buddha Thanh May 1, 1982)

Shakyamuni Buddha in the past said: Three stages of cultivating blessings of wisdom, Hundreds of kalpas of good generals. That is, in three Asanga kalpas he cultivated blessings and wisdom, and for hundreds of kalpas he cultivated good appearances. He practiced asceticism, doing things that were difficult for anyone else to do; Practice patience, endure things that people find difficult to endure. For the sake of sentient beings, he developed the mind of Bodhi, cultivated Omniscience, and did not spare his own life to teach and transform sentient beings. Life after life He patiently labors and suffers; eating things that people don't want to eat, giving in to things that people can't give in to. That's why he became Buddha and attained Bodhi.

Buddha did not become a Buddha by practicing one day and one night; He must practice for three kalpas of Asanga, then manifest the Eight Signs of Enlightenment (3). What are these Eight Signs of the Path? The first appearance is from the Tu Suat heaven. Tushita heaven is the place where the Dharma Prince preparing to become a Buddha resides. The second general is Tru Thai. While Buddha was in the womb, he always turned the Dharma wheel to teach and transform sentient beings, for the sake of all predestined sentient beings that he preached the Dharma. The third form is Xuat Thai. Buddha left the womb on the eighth day of the fourth month. After coming out of the womb, He pointed one hand to the sky and the other to the earth and said:

"Heaven above the world, I am the only one!"

Meaning:

"In heaven and on earth, there is no one more noble than me!"

Was the Buddha extremely arrogant and conceited? I am not Buddha's defense lawyer, but Buddha is truly a person worthy of such a title. When he was just born, he said that because he wanted to introduce sentient beings to understand the Way. The day Buddha was born, nine dragons sprayed water to bathe him; Growing up in the palace, he learned all worldly dharmas. He has learned all the human skills of life. He says he studies, but actually he understands without hindrance.

One day, he walked around the four gates of the city and saw the scenes of birth, old age, sickness, and death, so he realized that human life is full of suffering, experiencing birth, remaining, difference, and destruction, which are also creation, existence, destruction, and emptiness. Realizing that birth, old age, sickness, and death are truly full of afflictions and that human life has no meaning, he gave up his wealthy position and left; It is one of the Eight Marks of the Path.

Buddha's practice of Dau Da can be said to be the best. While at Tuyet Son Mountain, every day he practiced diligently, only eating one sesame seed to maintain his life, and never taking vitamins A, B, or C at all. Then he received goat's milk from a girl's making offerings and then went to the Bodhi tree to meditate and make vows saying: "If I cannot attain Perfect Enlightenment, I will definitely not stand up." Immediately after that, He sat for 49 days. By chance of maturity, in the middle of the night, he saw the morning star and realized the Way, suddenly realizing the state of no birth and no death, no increase or decrease, no dirt or cleanliness, pure nature, wonderful enlightenment of the true mind.

As disciples of Buddha in this Dharma Ending Age, we need to be true Buddhists. You must know that Buddha and the Patriarchs of the past practiced not easily. Now, although I don't have to eat a sesame seed every day, I just need to not be greedy for delicious food, vitamins, or nutrients. This body is a bundle of rotten flesh assembled by four great beings, and is of no value; Now, because of this stinky leather bag, I am a buffalo, a horse, a slave! I don't know how long I've been a slave like that, I don't know how much evil karma I've created, but I still haven't been "discovered and released." Not willing to see clearly and let go of it, still continuing to be a buffalo and horse; It's really worthless. So we have to return to our original roots.

Studying Buddha, practicing, is to clearly understand that human life is suffering, then attain Buddhahood, that is the real truth. So today, on Buddha's Birthday, we must follow Buddha's teachings, take Buddha's body as our body, Buddha's actions as our actions, Buddha's mind as our mind, Buddha's vow as our vow, Buddha's will as our will. You must be patient and learn without fear of hardship or suffering. If so, everyone will become a Buddha, attain enlightenment and escape birth and death.

Because he sought Omniscience, Buddha did not regret his life and developed a courageous spirit of practice. Now that I can't stand the hardships, how can I become a Buddha? When you leave the home life and do not truly practice, you truly betray the hearts of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas and Patriarchs! If one day the greed is not eliminated, the competitiveness is not suppressed, the desire for fame and profit is not destroyed, and selfishness and self-interest continue to grow, then how can we have the face to face the Buddha, our parents, and our ancestors? Don't think about yourself, but about others. Must practice diligently; Don't waste your time. The impermanence demon does not know when; When it comes, even if I want to live a few more days, I won't be able to do it:

"Ma invites the old man to study the Way,

She is an urban teenager."

Translated as:

"Don't wait for old age to practice,

The grave is full of bamboo shoots."

life, birth then death, death then birth; If you live unworthy, you will die as an animal. Once this body is lost, it will be difficult to recover for thousands of lifetimes. So don't deceive yourself, don't become a lawyer to defend yourself. Just think that there is no need to practice, one day Buddha will help you become a Buddha! Even Venerable Ananda is Buddha's younger brother, but Buddha could not give Samadhi to Ananda, but Ananda himself had to make an effort to practice.

Therefore, when you come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, you go to the Buddha Selection School (where you take the exam to become a Buddha); You have to study well so that when it comes time to take the exam, you can pass. Don't wait until you fail the exam, by then it will be too late to regret!

tieu_de: 12. BACH KIAO TIEN
tom_tat: When Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha left the royal palace to practice the Way, there were three people on his father's side, (4) two people on his mother's side followed him; But these people eventually left Buddha. What is fate like? Three people said Buddha practiced too hard, they endured...
noi_dung:
12. BACH KIAO TIEN

(Van Buddha Thanh May 1, 1982)

When Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha left the royal palace to practice the Way, there were three people on his father's side, (4) two people on his mother's side followed him; But these people eventually left Buddha. What is fate like? Three people said Buddha's practice was too hard, they couldn't bear it so they left Buddha to practice another method; And the other two people, when they saw Buddha drinking goat's milk, thought that Buddha did not suffer and was greedy for enjoyment, so they also left Buddha. Please try to observe: The nature of living beings is difficult to please; should say: "all Buddhas wish to satisfy sentient beings."

Living beings desire all kinds of things. Whenever you want something, you are greedy for it. There is no bottom in greed. So if you please them with one thing, they will crave something else. Greed is a bottomless bag of greed. At no time can this desire be satisfied; Stop being greedy for this and get greedy for that. When you are born, you already begin to be greedy; From childhood to adulthood, from youth to old age, from old age to death, the whole life is greed. If you are greedy for fame, you will die for fame; If you are greedy for profit, you will die for profit. Greed for fame will be burned to death by fire, greed for profit will be drowned by water; So those are the two disasters of water and fire. If you desire glory and wealth, you will die because of the wind. Those are the three disasters of life (Three Tai). Living beings value worldly things too much and refuse to let them go!

When Shakyamuni Buddha practiced, he knew how to endure hardship and work, yet his fellow believers left him to practice other pagan dharmas. Currently, we practice according to Buddha's Dharma, so there are many people who disagree, thinking that it is too much suffering and suffering too much loss. Those people do not have sincere hearts and do not make sincere wishes. Many people, after leaving the home life, only know how to eat and wait for death, not being able to understand their life and death issues, and then very casually scandalize themselves as the days pass. When the impermanence demon comes, there is nowhere to cling to, neither life nor death is free.

People leaving the home life like that are a waste of time. Don't think that if you follow Buddhism, you can freely create karma. If you think so, then you are a sinner. Shakyamuni Buddha practiced asceticism that others could not endure, so in the end he became enlightened and became a Buddha. At first he taught the Fourth Dharma

De: Suffering, Origin, Cessation, Path. There are three types of suffering (Three sufferings), eight types of suffering (Eight sufferings), and immeasurable suffering. The three types of suffering include suffering, suffering, and suffering.

What is suffering? That is, the suffering of the poor.

Suffering is the suffering of the rich.

Suffering is the suffering of those who are neither rich nor poor.

What is suffering, or the suffering of the poor? There is no house to live in, no warm clothes to cover the cold, no thin clothes to wear when it's hot, and no food to eat. That is an extremely miserable situation, suffering within suffering, suffering above suffering, ten thousand sufferings entwined together. Why must we suffer like that? Because in the past life we did not practice, or deceived our teachers to destroy our ancestors, or despised the Dharma, committed all kinds of evil karma, only listened to illusory fame and profit, listened to the cunning instigations of our own hearts, did not know how to practice, so we fell and suffered all that suffering. The vast majority of those who experience suffering are reincarnated as animals; Because in his previous life he blasphemed the Mahayana and deceived the master to destroy his ancestors, he fell into hell, then from hell he became a hungry ghost, then became an animal, and finally became a human. But as a human, the senses are incomplete and the five senses are not upright.

The second is suffering. That is the suffering not endured by the poor but the suffering of the rich. Rich people have perfect clothes, clothes, and houses; He had cars, ships, and all kinds of happiness, but suddenly he encountered a fire that destroyed all his belongings and left nothing. Or crashing a plane, or being on a boat and drowning in the sea, these are all sufferings. Being rich is of course good, but suddenly, when a disaster occurs, everything is gone, that is called "ruin." "Destructive" Here it is not about destroying suffering but about destroying one's blessings.

The third is Suffering, that is, the suffering that both rich and poor endure. Ordinary people, from childhood to adulthood, then from youth to old age, then old age to death, go through changes every minute and every second without being able to control themselves. When you get old, your eyes are blurry, your ears are deaf, and your arms and legs are no longer flexible. That is the form of Suffering.

The three sufferings above have great power in this world. All heroes and heroes cannot escape these sufferings, and even die from suffering. Do you think this is pitiful? "Good is rewarded with good, evil is rewarded with evil." Retribution is just a matter of sooner or later; Misfortunes and blessings as small as a feather never fail. So don't follow your nature and act arrogantly, creating all kinds of bad karma. One seventy years old hatred, Returning to the beginning of a hundred years! (When you stumble, you will regret forever. When you turn around, your life will be a hundred years old!)

world, no matter what we do, we need to have righteousness. People leaving the home life need to uphold the Dharma, practice the Dharma, always follow the orderly framework, and should not violate the precepts, no matter how small. If we are not careful, it is easy to create karma; so say: "The gate of hell before the Sangha." (The gates of hell are filled with monks.)

If a person leaving the home life does not keep the precepts and rules, they will definitely fall into hell, there are no exceptions! Because you already know clearly and still try to commit the crime, your crime will be three times higher than that of an ordinary person. This is no joke; Don't think that Buddha and Bodhisattva don't see what you do, then you can do whatever you want. Heaven knows what you think in your heart, let alone Buddha and Bodhisattva! Don't think that Buddha and Bodhisattva don't have eyes and then you're just going to mess up and act arrogantly. That's like "cynicism," Cover your ears, ring the bell, steal and then run away, thinking no one is listening. It's really self-deception. In the end, you will suffer retribution. By then, it will be too late to regret it.

tieu_de: 13. THE EIGHT Suffering
tom_tat: "The reason Wu has a great eunuch is because he has a body; The corn has no body, the corn has trouble?" Translate
noi_dung:
13. THE EIGHT Suffering

Lao Tzu said:

"The reason Wu has a great eunuch is because he has a body; The corn has no body, the corn has trouble?" Translated as:

"I have great misfortunes because I have this body. If I don't have my body, then why do misfortunes exist?"

People have all kinds of attachments but refuse to let go because they are locked in the cage of the Five Aggregates. Because of not being able to escape, within these Five Aggregates, all kinds of attachments, all kinds of discriminations, all kinds of delusions arise, and there is no way to escape birth and death.

In Buddhism, when talking about Suffering, I previously talked about the Three Sufferings; Now let's talk about the Eight Sufferings. This bowl of suffering covers eight types; In reality, there are not only eight sufferings, but there are boundless sufferings.

What is the Eight Sufferings? These are: Birth, old age, illness, death suffer, Love separates from suffering, Resentment increases, suffering arises, The five skandhas become suffering, Seeking to attain no suffering. These eight sufferings harm people in the world very much.

Birth suffering: Humans are born and already endure immense suffering. When I was still in my mother's womb, when I ate cold food, I felt like I was in a snowy mountain; When I eat hot food, I feel like I'm in a volcano. Then all kinds of unexpected things happened. When you are born, it is like being forced between two mountains; That's why when babies are born they cry loudly: "So miserable! So miserable!" That's because children want to complain but don't know how to speak so they just cry.

If a person does not have a body, there is no feeling of suffering at all, but when a person has a body, there are all kinds of painful feelings. So the moment of birth is like the moment a turtle is torn from its pubic area. Suffering is difficult to endure.

Death suffering: If there is birth, there must be death. At death, the Four Elements disperse and are blown away by the karma wind. That suffering is difficult to express.

Suffering: The human body is made up of earth, water, wind, and fire. If there is much fire then there is little water, if there is much wind there is little land, if there is much water then there is little fire. If the Four Great Elements are not coordinated or balanced, illness will naturally arise; If there is illness, there is pain.

People whose head hurts, their legs hurt, or their arms, back, spleen, stomach, kidneys... Every illness has its cause. If someone is fond of beauty, the kidneys will easily get sick; Those who are greedy for wealth will easily get sick in the heart, those who like to be angry will easily get sick in the liver, those who are sad will easily get sick in the lungs, those who harbor resentment will easily get sick in the spleen. Diseases of the heart, liver, spleen, lungs, and kidneys are all caused by hatred, resentment, anger, anger, and trouble. People with anger in mind damage the heart, people with strong resentment damage the spleen, people with sadness and worry damage the lungs, people with a lot of anger damage the liver, people with a lot of worries damage the kidneys. So if the Four Elements are not coordinated, they are caused by hatred, resentment, worry, anger, sadness, and lost emotions. If there is too much joy, too much resentment, too much sadness, too much fear, or too much desire, the Four Elements will become uncoordinated, giving rise to all kinds of illnesses. If you get sick, it's easy to get old, so after getting sick, old age comes.

Old man: When you get old, your eyes become dim, your ears become deaf, your teeth fall out, your legs shake, and your body can no longer stand steady.

Birth, old age, illness, and death are four types of suffering that make people not at peace, giving rise to all kinds of afflictions.

Farewell to suffering: Why am I human? Because I have love and love, I came to this world of Five Defects. If we have little love, we will not be born into this world, but will be born into the Ultimate Bliss World, the Lapis Lazuli World, or other worlds.

The ancients said: "Unimportant craving does not give birth to Saha, karma does not give birth to emptiness, Ultimate Bliss." (If love is not heavy, it will not give birth to Saha. If karma hindrances will not end, will it return to Ultimate Bliss?) When karma is gone, if love is empty, then you will become Buddha; Heavy karma, lots of love, that is, ordinary people. Ordinary people are confused by love, cannot break through the web of love, and think that love is the most noble. People believe that love between a man and a woman is a very precious thing. In fact, the stronger the love, the deeper the love, the more trapped you are in the cycle of ignorance. Some people know it's a trap but eventually fall in love. When boys and girls become adults, they only think about getting married quickly. It's so familiar with the old ways! "Ai" It's a kind of emotional attachment. Some people love money, some people love beauty. Money is something outside the body, beauty is felt in the heart. Attachment is also caused by love.

When the spirit is suffering, the mind is not at ease, and all kinds of discomfort are also due to this love. The suffering of separation is the suffering of separation when two people love each other. Two people who love each other like glue, like fish and water, suddenly something happens that causes them to reluctantly break up. They are in a situation where it is difficult to separate, difficult to part; Is there any suffering that is not easy to control, so it is called Love and separation from suffering.

Resentment increases and suffering: When I meet and talk to people with predestined relationships, I feel very compatible, working together is very easy, without conflicts. But there are people who, when they first meet, feel like they have no connection and want to hate them right away, so they try to avoid the other person and find another place to go. Who would have thought that when I went to another place, I would meet that person again! The more I hate them, the more I confront them. That is also a suffering.

Pray for suffering: There is desire because there is greed. Greed without satisfaction gives rise to afflictions, so that is also suffering. If you seek fame, fortune, money, or beauty but don't get it, you're miserable because it doesn't satisfy your wishes.

Getting what you want is not enough happiness. For example, if you haven't earned money yet, you're afraid you won't be able to earn it; When you earn it, you're afraid you'll lose it, so you're on guard day and night. Therefore, wishing to get something is already suffering, but not wanting to get it is even more suffering! Therefore, for other things, just follow this and deduce. If you don't have it, you're afraid you won't be able to get it. If you have it, you're afraid of losing it. These are all states of mind that are not calm, not free, not at peace.

The five skandhas of suffering: The five skandhas are form, feeling, perception, mental formations and consciousness; also called the Five Aggregates. It is something that is very difficult to subdue, it is very difficult to see it as empty. These five skandhas flare up like fire, burning our minds and causing us immense pain. If we have the Dharma of Peace of Mind and Dharma of Peace of Mind, then these eight sufferings cannot touch us; should say:

"The old monk himself possesses the Dharma of Peace,

Bat Kho sent the wild immortal into the room."

Translated as:

"The old monk originally had the magic of Peace of Mind,

Eight consecutive sufferings are of no use."

tieu_de: 14. TO PRACTICE DOESN'T NEED TO BE TOO SMART
tom_tat: I need to learn to be "naïve." But learning to be naive is not an easy thing, because experience often teaches you not to be naive. Therefore, if you nurture your mind like a fool, then that is called sophistication. Practicing means wanting to nurture…
noi_dung:
14. TO PRACTICE DOESN'T NEED TO BE TOO SMART

(Van Buddha Thanh May 7, 1982)

Lao Tzu said:

"Cultivate great and cunning lore, Learning originality is like a fool looking at water." Translated as:

"Nurturing a mind like a fool is a great skill, It's amazing to learn until it's like a daze."

I need to learn to be "naïve." But learning to be naive is not an easy thing, because experience often teaches you not to be naive. Therefore, if you nurture your mind like a fool, then that is called sophistication. Practicing practice means wanting to cultivate "doctrine," cultivate your mind like a fool; The dumber the better.

Why do you call it stupid? Stupidity means having absolutely no delusions. If you are not foolish, you will be full of false thoughts. If you have many delusions, you naturally want to find old stories, want to know current stories, then want to meddle in all kinds of nonsense, want to understand all kinds of promiscuous news articles. These are obstacles to practice. What is true stupidity and ignorance? That means entering Concentration. If one enters Samadhi, then east, west, south, and north are unknown; with the world without conflict, free and without hindrance.

Why can't I be free and fearless? That's because there is still fighting, greed, seeking, selfishness, and self-interest; Therefore, it is impossible to be free. Even if you want to be free, you can't do it. When you are dissatisfied with the present, dissatisfied with the past, dissatisfied with the future, thinking that others are not good to you, thinking that you treat others well, justifying yourself, standing on a position that is not inferior to anyone, that you are better than others, then you cannot practice the Way. Cultivating the Way means not making excuses, not being cunning, not talking nonsense; so say: Mahasattva, unforgiving, Amitabha Buddha, the ancestors. (Great Bodhisattva, does not interfere in other people's affairs. Amitabha Buddha, everyone takes care of their own business!)

Always guarding your body and mind, not thinking chaotically, that is truly cultivating the Way. People who do not truly practice the Tao are always thinking about this and that, always looking for ways to benefit themselves. Therefore, those who truly practice must: Ten thousand conditions are released, One thought does not arise. (Let go of everything, not even a single thought arises.) Let go of all fame, fortune, beauty, food, drink, and sleep. No thoughts arise, so there is no self, person, sentient being, or recipient; always be at ease and peaceful.

What is true freedom? That means not giving rise to false thoughts! If you keep giving rise to false thoughts every day, you will not have freedom; Your disordered thoughts will reach the ends of space, the Dharma Realm. If you don't want to practice, then there's no need to say anything. If you really want to practice, then don't think wildly, tie your mind tightly to one place, and be single-minded. Only when you are dedicated will you be inspired; Whenever the mind is distracted, it becomes dull. Therefore, those who want to practice must know this principle.

tieu_de: THE MONSTERS ATTACK ON MY BODY
tom_tat: People who come to Van Buddha Thanh to leave the home life do so voluntarily, not by necessity. Either American or Chinese, they all volunteered and prayed many times before being promised the ability to leave the home life. People who take refuge are the same, they go to Van...
noi_dung:
THE MONSTERS ATTACK ON MY BODY

(Van Buddha Thanh May 8, 1982)

People who come to Van Buddha Thanh to leave the home life do so voluntarily, not by necessity. Either American or Chinese, they all volunteered and prayed many times before being promised the ability to leave the home life. People who take refuge are the same. They come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas because they voluntarily want to take refuge. If they don't want to, no one will force them, because forcing is not the ultimate Dharma; so say: Forced to extract expenses through bad omens. (Melons picked reluctantly are not sweet.)

If a person does not voluntarily leave the home life, even if you let them become a monk, they will eventually return to the world. There are people who sincerely want to leave the home life, but after a long time they still lose their mind and return to the world, not to mention those who do not truly want to become a monk. Those are cases that can happen.

Leaving the home life is a brilliant story, the work of a great man, not the story of a thief, a coward, a petty person, or a petty person. As a person leaving the home life, you must clearly understand the duties of the person leaving the home life, be clearly aware of the position and mission of a monk, and do not hang out with the crowd like a secular person. Don't let people say yes then you say yes, people say go then you go, you don't have a direction, you don't perceive clearly.

Taking refuge in the Three Jewels or protecting the Three Jewels is the same; When you take refuge in the Three Jewels, you need to protect the Three Jewels. It's not like if you take refuge in the Three Jewels, you want the Three Jewels to protect you. Don't look for comfort in Buddhism. If you do, you will suffer later. If you regret it, it will be too late.

We are all full of delusions, delusions as numerous as dust particles. Why are there so many delusions? That's because there are many germs in our body, some big, some small, some old, some young. Some of those bacteria have supernatural powers, some have demonic powers, some have human powers, some have heavenly powers, some have earthly powers. Those worms were on my body, performing magic, creating evil and evil. They also know how to send telegrams! Every time they send a telegram to my mind, a false thought arises! So my delusions really never stop. As soon as this false thought subsides, another telegram is transmitted, causing another false thought to arise. These are all caused by the worms in your body.

Although these insects are insects, they are special agents! If there is something, there is supernatural power, that is, an agent from heaven; Some people know magical powers, that is, they are agents of the gods; Some things are known through human beings, that is, they are human agents; There are things called ghost power and animal birth power. If there is an insect that helps you practice to develop Bodhi mind, that is the insect that has Buddha's knowledge; There is a bug that calls people to do good deeds, that is Bodhisattva communication. In short, in the heavens and the earth, the myriad creatures, in the rooms, in the houses, in the void of the Dharma Realm, there is not a single species that is not born in one's own body.

Why do we take vitamins? It's because we want to nurture those germs; Nurture them until they become fat. Although we cannot eat those insects, they can eat our flesh. The Avatamsaka Sutra says: "The human body is made up of countless, countless bacteria accumulated." Think about it: The body is made up of each of these bacteria; Now I'm working as a servant for them, wanting to eat well, dress well, and live in a luxurious home. Isn't that crazy? There was a time when these germs had a meeting and made me sick. The doctor came to treat me, but the treatment did not cure me. At that moment, these insects clapped their hands and laughed. They are very excited because I have to surrender to them.
