Therefore, people who do not like to do good things, only want to do bad things, want to take advantage of them, are all led by evil insects. They prevent us from developing the Bodhi mind because they want to make us fall and make us lose confidence.

If you don't believe it, just try cutting your own meat with a knife! After a few days, these insects will become active again. That's why humans are so pitiful! Seeing your body as a precious gem, nurturing those insects, is truly a mistake. Those who believe I also say it, but those who don't believe I also say it. I say it to let these germs listen to let them know that there are people in this world who know their subtle activities!

tieu_de: 16. SECRETS OF PRACTICE: FOOD SECRETS AND FRUITS
tom_tat: The world has creation, existence, destruction, and emptiness; Human beings have birth, old age, illness, and death; that is natural morality. You should clearly understand this principle: When it becomes established, it will last, then it will perish, and then it will be empty; You will be born, you will get old, you will get sick, you will die...
noi_dung:
16. SECRETS OF PRACTICE: FOOD SECRETS AND FRUITS

(Van Buddha Thanh May 9, 1982)

The world has creation, existence, destruction, and emptiness; Human beings have birth, old age, illness, and death; that is natural morality. You should clearly understand this principle: When it becomes established, it will last, then it will perish, and then it will be empty; You will be born, you will get old, you will get sick, then you will die. If there is no city, there is no stability, no destruction, and no emptiness; If there is no birth, there is no old age, no illness, and no death.

But if we use false thoughts and attachments to distinguish this matter, then even after many eons we will not be able to distinguish clearly. No matter how much distinctions are made, it is confusing. As soon as he understood a little, he became confused, so he remained in the cycle of samsara and could not escape. If you want to escape samsara, you must destroy this path of delusion and delusion, only then can you practice and attain the Way, realizing the original Buddhahood, which has always been neither going nor coming, neither dirty nor clean, neither increasing nor decreasing, nor being born nor dying, there is nothing like sadness or affliction. All the Five Impurities and Six Impurities do not exist. But humans do not know how to let go of the false, so they cannot grasp the true; should say:

"The Immortal Immortal,

Become immortal;

Letting go of immortality,

Unexpectedly reborn".

Translated as:

"Don't throw away the fake

How can we get the real thing?

Don't let go of death

Why change to life?"

If you do not restrain your wild delusion, true wisdom will never appear. Self-nature is obscured by ignorance. Ignorance has two helpers, two plotters. What are they? The first is food, the second is beauty; One is called food, the other is called lust! These two things help ignorance do all kinds of bad things, so the book of Confucianism says: "Really, wild nature." That is, greed for food and lust for beauty are the nature of living beings. However, we must know why ignorance cannot be destroyed? Why can't afflictions be stopped? Why doesn't wisdom appear? That's because we have a greedy heart and a lustful heart!

Eating and drinking supports desire, and desire increases ignorance. People are born knowing how to eat, children are born knowing how to drink milk. If there is no milk, it cries, drinks it, then wants more. That's right! This greed is already present at birth, after the greed for food is born, the greed for beauty is born. Boys crave female lust, girls crave male lust, they are attached to each other, their desires do not let go, they cannot see through. Eating and drinking any kind of essence turns into essence. Whenever sperm is abundant, lust is born, so the ancients said: "Storm of lustful lust, coldness arises in the mind." (When you are full, you think about lust. When you are hungry and cold, you start stealing.) When you are full, a boy thinks of a girl, a girl thinks of a boy, only this thought of desire arises. When you're poor, you think about stealing, just to get something to eat. When you eat, then sex arises again. So when you eat enough nutrients and become fat and obese, lust only arises. People first develop greed for food, want to eat delicious food, want to eat to make their body strong. But eating a little is not enough, but eating a lot can satisfy your greed? That's why people die because of form and because of food. If ignorance is not real and form is a fabrication, it cannot harm anyone.

People leaving the home life eat food that is as bad as possible, and no nutrition is even better. So don't take the matter of eating too seriously. Eating is to maintain life and practice the Dharma; You don't need to have too many nutrients, but you also don't need to eat spoiled foods that make the body sick; that is practicing the Middle Way.

I really admire a person in Taiwan, that is the Venerable Thuy Qua, (5) He does not love money nor beauty. He did not even look at the offerings people made to Him. That is something that ordinary people cannot do, because no one can let go of greed, even considering money as life. But He was very gentle, disregarded money, offerings were piled up in one place, whoever wanted to take whatever they wanted, He did not pay attention, and let his disciples steal as much money as they wanted (the thieves later returned to the world). You see, did He manage money more strictly after that? That's not true! Not only does He not manage money, but even when looking, He doesn't even bother to look. You see how high His concentration is! He only eats fruits and peanuts, not any foods with flavors or cooked, stir-fried, or boiled foods. Because He did not enter according to form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or dharma, he attained the First Fruition of Arhat. His practice was very inspiring, so he often protected Taiwan. Some people recognized who He was, but there were also people who did not know His virtues, so they insulted Him, calling Him "Ayang Tang". (ignorant teacher).

This year, his body was weak, so he only ate a little porridge, but some people slandered him, saying that he had fallen into hell. Actually, those people don't understand and they are wrong. Whether or not to eat porridge is His business, so why bother trying to tease Him? If everyone practices like Venerable Thuy Qua, without greed or contamination, then the Buddha's teachings will definitely become clearer and more developed, and the Dharma will survive. He has made me extremely happy. He is a fellow practitioner of the same Way and is very compatible with me.

It cannot be said that everything in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is good, all is Buddha Dharma. But everyone here follows the Buddha Dharma and does not pay attention to eating well, dressing well, and living well; They only focus on how to maintain this fake Four Great Body to live, which is enough. Our need is the Dharma, the taste of the Supreme Dharma. That's why every day at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, there are Sutras and Dharma lectures. When listening to the Sutra, you need to be brave and diligent, wholeheartedly listen to the Avatamsaka Sutra, don't be lazy. You listen to the Sutra teachings not for the Master's sake, but for your own sake. If you knew everything, there would be no need to listen, but you don't know everything. What we know is Worldly Wisdom, intelligence that can distinguish and understand the life stories of ordinary people. Studying Buddha Dharma means studying for yourself, not for the Master or for others. Please remember, don't let time pass in vain, and if you regret it later, it will be too late.

tieu_de: EATING MEAT IS EATING PEOPLE
tom_tat: (Van Buddha Thanh, May 30, 1982) "Thousands of years of wrangling, deep resentment from a sea of hatred and trouble. Educating the world to fight with swords and soldiers, betraying the disciples and selling their voices!" Translate
noi_dung:
EATING MEAT IS EATING PEOPLE

(Van Buddha Thanh May 30, 1982)"Thousands of years of wrangling, Oan from the deep sea of hatred is difficult to reconcile. Educating the world to fight with swords and soldiers, betraying the disciples and selling their voices!" Translated as:

"Thousands of years of resentment are filled with soup, resentment is as deep as the ocean of hatred that is difficult to dissolve. If you want to know why there is war, listen to the slaughterhouse, at midnight!"

From ancient times until now, there have been many people who sacrificed the lives of others for their own benefit, willing to kill others to nourish themselves. Therefore, the piece of meat in the bowl of soup contains a resentment as deep as the ocean. From generation to generation, we kill each other and eat each other's flesh. All living beings want to live and fear death, but people still use oppressive tactics to massacre those weaker than themselves.

In the minds of the animals before they died, great resentment crystallized. They only wanted to seek revenge. There was no way to appease this idea of ​​hatred. Do you want to know where in the world the origin of war comes from? For example, the Vietnam War or the current war between Argentina and Great Britain? It's all because the karma is too heavy and too deep, so we use planes, artillery, battleships, and mines to destroy each other! If at night we listen in the butcher's house to the screams and groans of the pig, cow or goat begging for help, then we will know where the cause of war comes from. There is a poem that says:

"Humiliation" Self-reflection on the two individuals, Ly border on the periphery. Sentient beings are humiliated by sentient beings, Kind and considerate of human beings!" Translated as:

"In the word "humiliation" there are two people, one on the inside watching the other on the outside, Living beings eat living beings. If you think carefully, people eat people."

In Chinese, the word "flesh", meaning meat, includes the word "mouth". that is, the mouth opens, and the two words "human" i.e. two people: Inside there is a person and outside there is a person. People outside waiting for people inside. The person outside wants to go in but can't get in. The person inside wants to get out but can't get out because the person outside is blocking him, not allowing him to escape. So the word "humiliation" This is one who eats meat and one who is eaten. The predator is outside, and is a human being. The person being eaten is inside and is also a human being, but he has turned into an animal, and is also blocked from running out, unable to run up, not able to run down, as if he is surrounded, unable to escape. Even though the mouth was open quite wide, because the people outside had blocked it, the people inside couldn't escape the siege.

This enclosure can be a goat barn, a pig barn, or a cow barn or buffalo barn. The person being eaten is inside the cage, while the person eating the meat is outside and is prevented from leaving. Why don't you stop him from leaving? It's because I want to eat him! The person being eaten and the person eating the meat have a relationship: That is irreconcilable resentment!

Humans are living beings, the meat we eat is also living beings.

Whether it's an animal, a goat, a buffalo, a chicken, a horse, a dog, a pig, etc. are all one type of living being. If someone says that these animals were born from heaven for humans to eat, then who were humans born for them to eat? Therefore, animals are not necessarily born for humans to eat, but it is because humans rely on their superior minds that they eat animal meat. Therefore, this predatory relationship, if you think carefully, is cannibalism! If we say that people eat people, then try to ask how the person being eaten, (i.e. now transformed into a goat, into a pig, into a horse, etc.) has a relationship to you?

In the Shurangama Sutra, it is said: "The goat turned back into a human." If a goat can turn into a human, then all other animals can also turn into humans, just like you can change your head and face, but you don't know who that animal is. Do you know that animals such as goats, buffaloes, pigs, chickens, etc. Maybe those are all relatives, relatives of mine? If that relationship is so distant, let alone closer, then they know that they are their parents in a previous life, or their parents in this life, or their parents who don't know how many lives ago! Thinking like that, if one eats one's parents, it is truly filial. So if you think carefully, you will know that eating animal meat is actually eating human flesh!

If a person eats pork, the pig may turn into a human. When the pig becomes a human, it eats the pork that the other person transformed into. Cause and effect keep rotating, mutually eating each other: I eat it, it eats me. Therefore, the hatred becomes deeper and deeper; The deeper the hatred, the more you want to eat meat; The love of eating delicious food is guided by unjust karma, making you feel justified in killing the lives of others to supplement your own life!

If you don't believe me, let me tell you a true story: During the reign of Emperor Wu of Liang, Buddhism flourished. At that time, there was a person named Chi Cong, who was already enlightened (Minh Nhan Thien Tri Thuc). He can know the cause and effect of everything. At that time, Buddhism reached the point where the monks only chanted for people. Every family that has happy or sad events invites monks to chant auspicious sutras and chant auspicious mantras. One time, a rich man had his daughter's wedding, so he invited Chi Cong to chant sutras for blessings. Because the Buddha Dharma does not go beyond the world's dharma, the Patriarch also responded according to the customs of the world. As soon as he arrived at the house, he glanced at it and said: "Weird! Weird! Grandchild marries grandmother, Daughter eats mother, Son breaks father's skin, Pigs and goats sit on chairs, Relatives cook in pots, All living beings rejoice again, I feel so miserable!

Mr. Chi Cong said: "That's so 'weird'!" What's so weird? That's me marrying my grandmother! Because when the grandchild was just born, his grandmother got sick. When she was about to die, she held this grandson's hand and said that she was afraid that no one would care for him. Who would help him in the future to establish a karma family? Therefore, when the grandmother breathed her last breath, her hand was still holding her grandson, unable to bear her attachment. Grandma went down to the underworld to meet King Diem La, then wept and begged: "Dam La King! Please do me a favor: In this world, I have a young grandchild that no one cares for. Please let me go home and take care of him? King Yama was extremely compassionate and responded to the request, saying: "Okay, great! Go back to earth and take care of the boy. You are his grandmother, now you can return to be his wife, is that okay?"

That woman could not control her karma so she was reincarnated into the earthly world as a daughter. This daughter grew up and married that nephew. It's really a transformation, just a change of face and eyebrows, like trying on a new outfit and no one can recognize it. Only Mr. Chi Cong knew about that, so he said: "Weird! Weird! I'm marrying my grandmother."

Mr. Chi Cong saw his little girl eating a piece of pork and said: "Daughter eats mother." It's because this daughter's mother has done all kinds of heavy karma, so when she died, she was reincarnated as a pig; now killed by a butcher, cooked as a delicious dish and now this daughter eats her mother.

When He saw a boy in the back garden excitedly beating a donkey skin drum, He said: "The son beats his father's skin." It means that this boy's father was reincarnated as a donkey because he created karma, and when he died, people skinned him to make a drum; Now this child doesn't know that his father is a piece of skin made into a drum, so he only knows how to play the drum when he's happy.

Mr. Chi Cong went down to the row of seats, looked over and saw that the people sitting there were all buffaloes, cows, goats, etc. In the past, they were eaten by people, but now they have turned into humans and become relatives. The meats in the pot are all their relatives, so Mr. Chi Cong said: "You came here to party happily and joyfully to congratulate the landlord on your child's wedding. In truth, I find it truly miserable! Everyone is in mutual samsara, borrowing and repaying retribution, killing each other, eating each other; It's a suffering that's hard to describe."

After Mr. Chi Cong finished speaking, many people understood, and then made up their minds to become vegetarian, recite Buddha's name, and practice.

From ancient times until now, if you don't eat other people's meat, other people won't eat your meat either. Someone said: "No matter what you say, I won't believe it." If you don't believe it, I have no choice but to experiment and see!

18. TO CULTIVATE THE DAO NEEDS TO AVOID EVIL AND DO GOOD

(Van Buddha Thanh May 30, 1982)

"The origin of evil karma,

Due to beginningless greed, anger and ignorance,

The origin of the body, speech, and mind,

Necessarily fall into the golden stage repentance."

Translated as:

"All evil karma created from the past, Due to beginningless greed, anger, ignorance, arose from body, speech and mind. I now ask for repentance for all of them."

From ancient times until now, we have created karma, some evil and some good; Good and evil are not clearly mixed together. So sometimes we give birth to good thoughts, and sometimes we give birth to evil thoughts. A good thought "does not do evil but does all good." But when evil thoughts arise, they only think "do all evil, do no good."

Because from countless eons until now, good and evil have been mixed like this, so today we do good but tomorrow we want to do evil, and the day after tomorrow we create something that is neither good nor evil. When we practice the Way, it is difficult to escape karma. So sometimes we want to practice, sometimes we don't want to practice, sometimes we want to be pure, sometimes we want to be impure. Just let the waves push you, not knowing where you'll go. It's all due to the ideas that arose in the past and are now coming to fruition. There is the initial thought of wanting to practice, and the later thought of wanting to return to the secular world; The former idea wants to propagate Buddha Dharma, but the latter idea wants to destroy Buddha Dharma. It's extremely complicated. So what to do? Then it is necessary to learn the wisdom of Prajna; means:

"Trach Thien Nhi Tung,

Non-good rules reform.

Thi Dao Tac Tien Tien,

Non-Dao is rotten!"

Translated as:

"Choose what is good and follow it,

If something is bad, fix it.

If it is the Way then move forward,

If it is not the Way, then retreat!"

We must always be vigilant as if walking on the edge of an abyss, just like walking on thin ice. Practicing requires such extreme care! Should say: Sai chi chi ly, ma chi chi thien ly. (An error of one inch goes a mile.)

Therefore, practicing is: "Movement and behavior control self-esteem. Do not leave home when you act, stand, sit, or lie down". Don't give rise to contaminated thoughts, don't give rise to dark thoughts. Be very careful in every thought, every thought. If each idea is good, the more light it has, if the idea is evil, the more darkness it has. Good people have white aura, evil people have only black gas. Therefore, doing good or evil naturally manifests in one's appearance.

You can deceive people but you cannot fool demons, gods, Buddha, Bodhisattva. Therefore, regardless of whether the person is leaving the home life or the person who is lying, if he deceives like that, he will only create bad karma and has no merit to Buddhism. We must understand why, for countless lifetimes until now, we have not escaped the suffering of samsara of birth and death, always being so confused and stupid? It's because of the "bank account" His is not clear; Full of mixed things, half of the pure and impure, so samsara cannot leave the Six Paths! If we want to truly practice and become a Buddha, then before becoming a Buddha we must be courageous and diligent, not careless. It is important to know that: A day has passed, the network is gradually decreasing, like a fish out of water, what's the fun? The masses! Be diligent, like your head is burned. Just remember impermanence, don't be careless.

Some people are skeptical: "Is there really a King of Hell and a real demon impermanence (God of Death)?" That must be considered whether you can not die or not? If you can not die, that means there is no impermanence demon. If you have great abilities and do not receive retribution, it means there is no King of Yama. Can you not die? If that is not possible, then of course there is King Yama and the impermanence demon; Don't think that you are very smart, "cover your ears and steal the bell, ring the bell and run" deceive yourself. You must know, for countless eons up to now, because we do not believe in the existence of King Yama or impermanence, we have been in the Six Paths of samsara, going back and forth, with no way to escape the cycle of birth and death!

tieu_de: WHEN THOUGH THERE WERE HONORABLE PEOPLE
tom_tat: (Van Buddha Thanh June 5, 1982) "Human hearts are not the same as before, Morality has declined.
noi_dung:
WHEN THOUGH THERE WERE HONORABLE PEOPLE

(Van Buddha Thanh June 5, 1982)"People's hearts are not the same as before, Morality has degenerated."

The world today does not know how to progress but is increasingly going downhill. In the past, there weren't many schools or many readers, but people didn't have many crazy and corrupt things. Currently, the school has an unknown number of students, but there are more and more bad guys in the world.

The ancients learned mainly for reason, that is, to clearly understand human morality, how to not do evil, how to always do good, how to be filial to parents, have love for brothers, be loyal to the country, be faithful to friends, be polite to everyone, be kind to the nation, be honest in work and be ashamed of yourself. Nowadays, people go to school for fame and fortune!

The Chinese words Ming Li and Fame and Loi have the same pronunciation, but in reality the meanings are completely different. Those who study for fame and fortune only want to study any subject to make a lot of money. Just like there are people who want to study medicine or science, but only think that they will make a lot of money, not thinking that I study because I want the future to bring happiness to people, that I study medicine because I want to save lives and benefit others.

Currently, most students only know how to benefit themselves and do not know how to benefit others. There are also professors who openly encourage students to smoke drugs, engage in promiscuity, or cause all sorts of disturbances in the world. So the world is becoming more and more degenerate. Lao Tzu said:

"The Great Way has no humanity,

Wisdom emerges from the great puppet,

The six bodies are discordant and filial,

The country is in chaos, right and loyal."

Meaning:

"When the Great Way disappears, the merciful appear,

Wise people come, liars abound,

When families are in discord, filial people are born,

When the country is in chaos, there are loyal officials."

When the great Tao no longer exists, people will talk about humanity and righteousness. If the Great Tao existed, no one would talk about benevolence, because benevolence and righteousness would already be included in the Great Tao. When a wise person is born, of course there are fake people who also appear to deceive others. When a family is in harmony with each other and no one disputes, then of course the father is kind, the children are filial, the brothers happily live together, and the family is very happy. But if six families and relatives are in discord; If the father is not kind, filial children will be born. Just like in Mr. Thuan's time: The father is obedient, the mother is lewd, the younger brother is arrogant, but Shun is extremely filial. (Father stubborn, mother lewd, younger sister arrogant; However, Mr. Thuan wholeheartedly fulfilled his filial piety.)

King Shun's father was very stubborn. His name is Co Tau (blind old man), meaning that although he has eyes, he does not have eyes, because he does not know black and white, right or wrong, straight or crooked, good or evil. He had a son, King Thuan, a very filial son that he didn't even know. King Shun's mother was his stepmother; This woman is lustful, sinister, never talks about morality, only thinks about immorality. Mr. Thuan has a younger brother from another mother named Tuong who is also very arrogant and does not respect his brother. However, in his family, Mr. Thuan is extremely filial to his parents, loves and cares for his younger siblings.

At that time, Mr. Thuan's younger brother and his stepmother thought of a way to harm him, so one day they called him into the rice warehouse to clean up. Waiting until he went inside, Tuong immediately set fire to the house. The warehouse caught fire and burned fiercely. At that time, they thought that Mr. Thuan would be burned to death by fire, so the two of them left, extremely happy. But soon Mr. Thuan returned home. The younger brother was extremely surprised and asked: "You were in the warehouse cleaning, why didn't you get burned to death when the house caught fire?" Mr. Thuan replied: "When I saw the fire burning, I picked up two grass baskets to cover myself, then climbed onto the roof and jumped out, so I was neither hurt nor burned."

Another time, when Mr. Thuan went to the well to get water, those two people thought of a way to harm him. When Mr. Thuan climbed down the well, they brought a large rock to block the mouth of the well, preventing him from going up. They believe that Mr. Thuan will die this time. (There is a proverb that says "losing the province to the stone," meaning to fall into a well and then cover it with a stone, that is, to harm someone who is at the end of their path, comes from this dictionary.)

However, at the bottom of the well there is a cave! After Mr. Thuan went down to the well, he crawled up from that cave (some people say that in this tunnel there is a white fox that often visits there; It came to save Mr. Thuan). Although those two people always tried to harm him, Mr. Thuan never got angry, was always very filial to his parents and loved his younger brother very much.

At that time, Tuong thought that Mr. Thuan was dead, so he went home to tell his parents about dividing the inheritance. Y said: "Nuu Duong's parents, I love my parents, my husband, my father, my father, my second sister-in-law." example to say: "Goats and cows are left to parents, food is also left to parents. I don't need those things, I just want Mr. Thuan's zither, Mr. Thuan's flute, and Mr. Thuan's martial arts training items. Those are the things I want. I also want Mr. Thuan's two wives; Tell those two people to serve me again." (Mr. Thuan has two wives; One is named Nga Hoang, the other is named Nu Anh, these two are both daughters of King Nghieu. King Yao specifically promised to marry these two people to serve Mr. Thuan.)

Tuong finished speaking and went into Mr. Thuan's room. But as soon as I entered, I saw Mr. Thuan sitting on the bed. The statue was so scared, he thought that Mr. Thuan's soul had appeared. Mr. Thuan immediately spoke to comfort his younger brother not to be afraid.

During the time of Nghieu Thuan, people's hearts were so bad, but Mr. Thuan still did his best to fulfill his filial piety and filial piety. So it is said that in a family, if relatives of the six families do not get along, there will be a filial person born.

When the country is in chaos, a loyal loyalist appears. When the country is peaceful and unscathed, it is difficult to see loyal officials. When the country is in chaos, you can see who is loyal and who is a traitor very easily.

During the Song Dynasty, there were two dynasties, the Southern and the Northern. When the country was in utter chaos, the traitor Tan Coi appeared. Qin Hui killed Yue Fei; But Nhac Phi has been famous for thousands of years, while Tan Coi has had a bad reputation for thousands of years. Therefore "preserving the name of ancient times" and "eternal migration" are all names, but one is a good name, the other is a bad name. Just like in the Southern Song Dynasty, there was Mr. Van Thien Tuong; When the country was extremely chaotic, he was extremely loyal to Song. From beginning to end he defended the nation, refusing to surrender; that is a loyal minister. That's why when a country is in chaos, loyal officials can appear.

Right now, when we are building an ashram, it is also a time of great suffering and hardship. It is at this moment that we can see who is real and who is fake. A true dharma protector takes Buddhism as his duty; Take the care of the Three Jewels as your own responsibility.

Now the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is growing day by day, needing many people to support, needing many people to cooperate. Those who have strength will work hard, those who have material wealth will help with material wealth. You should not have the attitude of "sitting indifferently," I look at him, he looks at me; Because like that, we will never be able to do our best to contribute to Buddhism. We must take the propagation of Buddha's teachings as our personal duty, and maintaining the Buddha's teachings is the responsibility of each person. If so, Buddhism will definitely develop brilliantly in the future.

tieu_de: 20. TO CULTIVATE THE DAO NEEDS TO HAVE A PATIENT AND UNCHANGEABLE MIND
tom_tat: The trunk of the tree grows taller and taller every day, but we do not see the growth of the tree. Even though we don't pay attention, the tree keeps growing taller and taller, waiting ten or hundred years later, then the tree turns into a living thing.
noi_dung:
20. TO CULTIVATE THE DAO NEEDS TO HAVE A PATIENT AND UNCHANGEABLE MIND

(Van Buddha Thanh June 6, 1982)

The trunk of the tree grows taller and taller every day, but we do not see the growth of the tree. Even though we don't pay attention, the tree keeps growing taller and taller, waiting for ten or hundred years to turn into a useful object.

Trees are like that, people cultivating the Way are like that. Don't be too hasty, don't think that if you practice today, you will be enlightened tomorrow. It's not that easy! But you need to practice every day, improve every day, regardless of whether you make progress or not. Not retreating means progress. Just reducing delusions every day is already progress; If you meditate a little every day, that is progress; Every day when greed, anger and ignorance recede, it means progress; Don't want to rush. So say:

"If you move forward, you will quickly retreat."

Meaning:

"The faster you advance, the faster you retreat."

Going forward quickly means retreating quickly, so we need to have a constant mind to practice, and must repentance every day to correct mistakes:

"A single day cannot be improved, that is, a single day cannot be created".

Meaning:

"A day without correcting mistakes is a day without creating merit."

Therefore, to practice, we need to eliminate bad habits and mistakes, get rid of erroneous thoughts, and let our inherent bright wisdom appear. Everyone has this clear wisdom, but unfortunately it is obscured by ignorance. When you cannot use this clear wisdom, because ignorance covers it, it will make you want to go down, not want to go up; If we can reveal our wisdom, we will naturally move forward and up forever. That's called "reverse current" (go against the current)!

So practicing is not just a day or a night, but requires hours and minutes every day. Mornings are the same, afternoons are the same, year after month, practice is like that, always unchanging. It took a long time for me to cultivate the wisdom of Prajna. Don't be "one day hot and ten days cold," If you practice for ten days a day, you won't be able to achieve it. We must be like a tree trunk, growing a little more each day, practicing with sincerity every day.

During the period of practice, if you encounter any realm, whether it is demonic obstacles or adverse conditions or favorable conditions..., you must be calm and peaceful. Whether in favorable or unfavorable circumstances, we must be diligent, considering all things as if they are telling us the wonderful Dharma. If you understand that everything teaches the Dharma to you, every event is a Dharma lesson, then you will know the magic that language cannot describe. If you understand that, you will know the "original face" yourself, you know the way home. Therefore, by borrowing the world's dharma, we can go beyond the world's dharma, not being confused by all dharmas, not being confused by all appearances. When all realms come, if you are calm and clear, without obstacles, your wisdom will appear over time.

The reason why wisdom doesn't manifest is because we don't want to step forward and practice; just want to retreat! When encountering good fate, you will doubt and not make a decision. When encountering bad fate, you will immediately run after it. So forever wandering in the Six Paths of Samsara, with no way to escape. The more you are trapped, the deeper you go, the deeper you get, the more your feet sink and you can't get out. So if you see clearly, you can't let go, and ultimately you can't achieve liberation. Therefore, one is born and then dies, and dies and then is born again. A confused person is born, a confused person dies, during that time I don't know what to do, it's just crazy things, I can't find a good reason.

You guys! If so, human life is a confused life; It's all about fame, profit, and your own success. In fact, what the worldly people consider success, the Saints and Sages consider failure. Therefore, if you have debt, you must try to pay it off properly. I have to be a completely wise person. When you are wise, you must be wise forever, so you can break through the door of life and death and get out of the cycle of samsara. That is the way of a great man.

21. EAGLE OF THE GIRLS

(Van Buddha Thanh June 6, 1982)"Kim Chi bird's fate, The flesh and bones are completely destroyed,

Only the unchangeable mind exists,

Shining bright light.

The Dragon King holds the pearl,

Able to destroy the darkness of the millennium.

Turning the Wheel to attain the Buddhahood,

Ability to save from disaster.

Like the union in the middle,

I can't see Nhat Thuong Nhi!"

Translated as:

"The Eagle is dead,

Bones and meat are digested cleanly,

But the heart does not dissipate,

Bright round light.

The Dragon King took it as a jade,

Breaking through thousands of years of darkness.

Turning the wheel is like a mound,

Save from hundreds of misfortunes.

As in humans,

The day I used it, I didn't see it!"

That is a poem written by Venerable Ham Son; This verse is one of six verses praising the human mind. We all know that the Golden Eagle, when it spreads its wings, can cover yojana (a small yojana is 40 miles, a middle yojana is 60 miles, a great yojana is 80 miles). When the Eagle flaps its wings, it can make the sea water completely dry and clean. It can flap its wings to move sea water to another place, so we can see its immense power. But the Eagle will one day die. When it dies, all the bones are destroyed, but only the heart is not destroyed.

How does this Eagle eat and drink? It specializes in eating dragons. Dragons are creatures that have magical powers, can turn big, can turn small, can be invisible, and can manifest themselves. But when the dragon sees the Eagle, no matter how it has magical powers, it will give up. The only way is to wait for the Eagle to come and eat it. Therefore, when the Eagle ate too much dragon meat, the dragon king had no choice but to ask Buddha for help. He complained to Buddha: "If Eagles continue to eat dragons like this, our dragon species will soon be completely extinct; Buddha, please think of a way to help, so that the Eagle does not eat all the dragons."

Buddha immediately spoke the Dharma to the Eagle, teaching it: "From here onwards

You can't eat dragon meat anymore." Eagle replied: "If I don't eat dragon meat, how will I live?" Buddha recently taught: "I will teach my disciples to make offerings for you to eat every day when it's time to eat!"

Therefore, before people leave the home life, they make offerings to the Eagle, called alms giving (i.e. giving food to the Eagle). This is the verse recited at that time:

"The Golden Eagle,

Wild ghosts and gods,

Rakshasa demon mother,

Nectar is full of energy."

Translation:

"The Golden Eagle,

Demons in the wild,

Mother demon Rakshasa,

Full of nectar water.

When you offer food to this Golden Bird, you also offer it to the ghosts and spirits in the wild and the Rakshasa mother and child. "Wild" that is, a desolate, uninhabited place; Big trees and dense forests are where ghosts and spirits live. A mother and child of a demon species appeared, unable to eat anything in the world, only specializing in eating newborn babies. They think that baby meat is very soft, very fragrant, full of nutrients, and compared to vitamins, it is much more effective!

The demon mother had a thousand children, all of whom loved baby meat. If children were eaten by them, humanity would soon become extinct, so Buddha could not stand by and watch. He then used his supernatural powers to capture the youngest child of the demon mother and hid it in his alms bowl. When the mother returned from eating the baby meat, she discovered that her youngest child was missing. Because she also had supernatural powers, she knew that Buddha had captured him. She went to question Buddha and said: "Why did you kidnap my child for no reason?"

Buddha taught that: "Do you also know that you need your child? If you look for someone else's child to eat, whose child will someone else find to eat?" The demon mother said:" I eat meat to preserve my life. Now you kidnapped my child, but you don't eat him, so why did you kidnap him?"

Buddha said: "She knows that she needs her children, and everyone in the human world needs their children. If she ate other people's children, those people would feel extremely sad in their hearts. From now on, you are not allowed to eat children anymore!"

Demon mother said: "If I don't eat them, I have nothing to eat, so do you want to starve me to death?"

Buddha taught that: "It's okay! She cannot starve to death. I will teach my disciples that every time they eat a meal, they should set aside a portion of food to offer to her; From now on, you are not allowed to eat children anymore!"

From then on, this Rakshasa demon mother changed evil for good and stopped eating children.

"Nectar is full of abundance" This means that for eagles, or ghosts in the wild, or demon mothers, we all use the Nectar making offerings to make them full and happy. So people leaving the home life every time they eat lunch, they recite the mantra making offerings Giving food, because of such conditions.

The Eagle is very powerful when alive, but when it dies, its bones and flesh are destroyed, returning to the Four Elements (earth, water, wind, fire). However, the heart is not lost; Even if it is burned by fire or drowned by water, it will not be destroyed, but will remain the same as before. This heart is round and can emit bright light. If the dragon king gets this heart, it becomes a dragon pearl (Dragon pearl). When placing this pearl in the Dragon Palace, the Dragon Palace will emit a bright aura. If the Wheel-Turning King gets this heart, he can turn it into a gem like a mound of jewels to save all disasters and tribulations, with inconceivable magical powers. However, do we humans not have any part in this precious gem? No! Each of us has a priceless pearl! This gem like a mound exists in each person's nature, but is obscured by ignorance, causing it to fade away and unable to release its light. No matter how hard I tried, I couldn't find it, so the gem couldn't be used. That is a very sad thing!

People in this world keep abandoning their roots and chasing after the tops, turning their backs on enlightenment, blending with the dust of the world, refusing to return to their original duties, not wanting to let go of the worldly burdens to return to the shore of enlightenment. That's why each founder of a religion is very dedicated and dedicated to educating humanity, just to teach themselves to borrow the false to cultivate the truth, to leave ignorance to enlightenment, to return to the origin, to realize the "local light". your own, your precious inheritance that is full of jade like that.

However, we all want to pursue external things without knowing how to turn back and look inside to find the answer within ourselves. Therefore, life after life is always lost in the sea of suffering. There are people who want to practice but cannot let go of the desire to enjoy and be happy; Therefore, from beginning to end, I do not want to return to purity and let go of worldly attachments. That is truly pitiful!

tieu_de: LIFE, LOVE, RICH, AND ALL ARE NOT OUT OF SAMSARA
tom_tat: Look at historical examples of the richest, the most luxurious, the poorest, and the meanest
noi_dung:
LIFE, LOVE, RICH, AND ALL ARE NOT OUT OF SAMSARA

(Van Buddha Thanh June 6, 1982)

Just look at these historical examples of the richest, the most luxurious, the poorest, and the meanest:

"Thach Sung is rich, Pham Dung and Van Van Cam La, Thai Cong Tao, Bang To has a long life, Nhan has a short life, Luc Nhan Do in Ngu Hanh middle."Translated as:

"Thach Sung is rich, Pham Dung is poor, Cam La is late, Thai Cong is early, Bang To lives long, Nhan Uyen dies prematurely, Six people lie down, within the Five Elements."

In the past, the richest man was Thach Sung, a member of the Jin Dynasty; People called him "rich enough to rival the country", as rich as the whole country. One time, Thach Sung and his friend had a party, and his friend took out a two-foot-eight-inch tall coral tree from the warehouse for Thach Sung to see. Thach Sung looked and said: "This is not worth anything!" He immediately used his foot to crush the coral tree. The extremely sad friend said: "I don't know where to find such a precious thing as this coral tree. It's such a pity to have you crush it like that!" Thach Sung said: "What are you sorry for! What is that worth? My house is full of that trash, please come to my house and see!" This friend immediately went to the house to take a look, and sure enough, in Thach Sung's house there were hundreds of coral trees three meters high. Thach Sung said: "You can take it as you like, take whatever you like!"

Therefore, the thing that a friend considers precious is of no value to Thach Sung. That is to say that he is extremely rich, there is no way to know.

Pham Dung is a beggar who has nothing. Every day I have to beg, I eat as much as I get, I refuse to go out to work, and after I eat I have to beg again. So say:

"The family cannot afford a salary,

The body is without a hammer."

Meaning:

"There's no food in the house to eat the next day. I don't have a place to set up a mace."

Wherever he goes, that place is home. Although he was very poor and had to go out to beg for food, he later managed to collect a little food. Once Confucius and his students were starved of food in the Tran country. Because they had nothing to eat, Confucius sent someone to Pham Dung's house to borrow rice. You see! Confucius was a man with many disciples and now he had to go to a beggar to ask for rice. Isn't that funny?

At that time, Tu Lo followed Confucius' teachings and went to Pham Dung's house and said: "My teacher currently has no food, because the Tran country ran out of food, so I came here to borrow some rice."

Pham Dung says: "You can borrow rice if you want, but I have a few questions to ask you. If you can't answer, I won't lend it." Tu Lo, filled with confidence, said: " Okay, just ask!"

Pham Dung asked: "Please tell me: In heaven and earth, what is more, what is less; what is happy, what is sad; If you answer correctly, I will lend you rice unconditionally; If you answer incorrectly, I won't lend you rice. That is what I must make a clear agreement."

Tu Lo says: "The question is so easy, it's so simple! In heaven and earth, the stars are many but the moon is few; Happiness is when people get married, sadness is when people die."

After listening, Pham Dung waved his hand and said: "That's not true! That's not right!" Tu Lo realized that his answer was perfect, correct, and there was no better answer. He said that because Pham Dung did not want to lend rice, he tried to refuse; But he had no other choice, so he angrily left. When he met Confucius, he said: "Teacher! This guy Pham Dung is so disgusting and doesn't know any morality!" After that, Tu Lo recounted the responses of both sides to Confucius. Confucius heard this and said: "You answered wrong!" Tu Lo was extremely surprised and asked again: "Pham Dung said I was wrong because he stood on his own position. You have to stand on my position and say, why do you also say I answered wrong?"

Confucius replied: "Listen to what I say: In heaven and earth, petty people are many but noble people are few; When you're happy it's time to lend it to others, when you're sad it's time to borrow it from others! Please go back to Pham Dung and say so."

At that time, Tu Lo returned to Pham Dung's house and repeated Confucius' words. After listening, Pham Dung immediately realized that the answer was extremely accurate, so he took the rice to Tu Lo to borrow. He filled a load of rice for Tu Lo to carry back. But this burden is a treasure. Once put in, the rice will never run out. The more you use it, the more it will fill up; said that the poor also have treasures!

During the reign of Qin Shi Huang, there was a man named Cam La, who at the age of 12 became Prime Minister; but that was three years late, he should have been Prime Minister at the age of 9. Khuong Tu Nha was 80 years old when he met Vuong Van; So it was three years early, he should have met Van Vuong at the age of 83. Cam La was young and became Prime Minister, but Khuong Tu Nha did not meet King Van until he was very old!

Pang To lived to be more than 800 years old, so he had a very long life; But Nhan Uyen, a disciple of Confucius, only lived to be 30 years old and then died, so it was called a short life. Although Nhan Uyen's life was short, among Confucius's disciples, he was the most intelligent. He was also the most studious person, he only needed to hear one to know ten, while Tu Cong could only know two after hearing one. When Nhan Uyen passed away, Confucius felt extremely sorry and said: "Heaven's funeral remains! Heavenly burial left over!". Italy says: God has made my religion disappear! God has made my religion disappear!

Some of these six people are extremely rich, some are extremely poor, some have a high position early on, some reach noble status late, some live a long life, some die early, but these six people cannot escape the destiny of the Five Elements (metal, wood, water, fire, earth). They are all in the cycle of the Five Elements, rotating back and forth, circulating in the cycle of samsara; so say: "Human life is like a virtual dream, like a dew drop on a leaf, like lightning. Always reflect like that, and don't be attached!" At that time, I will have no worries. Practicing and knowing how to see clearly and then let go is even better. If you can't let go of everything at once, you have to let go step by step, thing by thing. Don't be attached

What is Samsara doing forever in the Six Paths?

tieu_de: 23. THE WANMA DOES NOT RETURN THE BODHISATTVA MIND
tom_tat: (Van Buddha Thanh, June 19, 1982) "If you study well, you will be punished harshly. If you become a Buddha, you will be immortal." Translate
noi_dung:
23. THE WANMA DOES NOT RETURN THE BODHISATTVA MIND

(Van Buddha Thanh June 19, 1982)"If you study well, you will be punished harshly. You will become a Buddha, and you will be immortal." Translated as:

"If you want to study well, you will find hardship. If you want to become a Buddha, you will first meet the devil."

"If you want to study well, you will find hardship." If you want to do good things, no matter what, evil will come to find you. The better you do, the harder the evil one will hunt you because it wants to settle your debt!

From countless lives up to now, life after life we have created mixed good and evil karma, with no clarity; That's why when you want to practice the Way, your creditors will come to you to collect their debts. For example, someone borrowed money from someone else and didn't pay it back properly. When he was not yet wealthy, the creditors knew he had no money so they did not come to collect; But when he became rich, the creditor immediately knocked on the door to collect his debt. Why? Because the creditor knows he has money! If he doesn't come to claim it, he won't know when he can claim it, so he has to claim it.

Therefore, in the process of cultivating the Way, we will encounter adversity, and when we encounter adversity, we must be more courageous and diligent, without losing our Bodhi mind. We must pay all the debts that the creditor comes to collect; That is, bringing your merit of practice and dedicating merit to creditors, to those who resent you, and to your relatives; so that when they receive their merit, they will be free from suffering and gain happiness, will be free from birth and death, and only then will their debt be completely wiped away.

From countless lifetimes until now, due to all kinds of causes and conditions, I have owed quite a lot. In this life, try to think critically about how many lives you have killed? How many unjust things have I created? Regarding sentient beings, if we have not killed any living creatures, such as lions, elephants, pigs, chickens, buffaloes, cows, etc. But it's very possible that I killed smaller creatures like flies, mosquitoes, crickets, lizards... Even though I say I have never killed such small creatures, I definitely still have the thought of killing living in my heart.

When I was young, because I didn't pay attention, I accidentally killed a lot of small insects. That's called the crime of ignorance, the crime of killing without intention. But the living beings whose lives we took away, now, when we want to practice the Way, will definitely come looking to collect our debt. This kind of debt is not just one or two, but countless, because life after life we accumulate it, too much to count!

Therefore, do not say that God is unjust: "I'm practicing now. I don't want to accept all the karma and debts from the past." If we think like that, we will never be able to attain the Tao, because our hearts are not fair. If we have a fair heart, we must accept the debt. So say: "If you want to study well, you will find it harshly"; When I suddenly become rich, my poor friends all come knocking on my door to collect debt.

"If you want to become a Buddha, you must first meet a ghost." Buddha attained enlightenment thanks to the help of demons. If there were no demons, there would be no Buddha. Demons come to test and make progress; should say: Desire and heavenly reason, The upper wing of the first floor. (If you want to see the end of a thousand miles, you have to climb one more floor.)

Let's take a look at "Fire Monkey" Is mine enough? If it is enough, then even if a thousand ghosts come, you will not change, if a thousand ghosts come, you will not retreat, you will not lose the Bodhi mind. The more suffering and hardship, the more diligent you are. No matter how complicated and confusing the adversities are, the mind must be even more peaceful and calm. Don't think it's unfair, don't complain about heaven or blame people.

When faced with adversity, accept it and practice the Paramita of patience. That's the practice that we have to practice. When the demons return, we don't have to confront them. It doesn't matter if we just endure a little more suffering; We must make vows to save those demons, make them take refuge in the Three Jewels, and develop the mind of Bodhisattva. The same goes for everyone, don't give birth to resentment, then you can turn swords and spears into jade, turn hatred into peace. Therefore, we must always look for the good in the bad of things. So say:

"Acts are not successful, Tac opposes selfishness. " (If you don't finish it, you have to go back and find it.)

Never be a lawyer defending yourself, no matter what happens, think:

"True acceptance of self-denial,

Discourse on other people's non-existence.

Tha phi means self phi,

In the same name as Great Compassion"

Translated as:

"Admit that you're wrong,

Don't pay attention to other people's mistakes.

Someone else's fault is my fault,

The same body means Great Compassion."

Because they are one, they cover demons. Demons are a part of the self. If there are demons in our own nature, then we can let the outside demons intrude. If the self-nature does not have demons, outside demons have no way to enter. What is the demon's self-nature? That means greed, anger, ignorance! Nhuoc no meow really good, Tac no move can help. (If the cat's food bowl is left out, no flies will come.)

When you know you're still "cloudy" then the devil tries to find a way to "surplus cloudy water and let the fish go fishing," want to cause chaos, want to reveal the "magic power" its. Therefore, every gesture, action, word, and thought must be very sincere: "Speech must be faithful, actions must be respectful." (Speech must be honest and faithful, actions must be completely respectful.)

Do not tell lies. Not daring to admit mistakes, always covering up their own mistakes: That is not the behavior of a person cultivating the Tao. Therefore, we must be very sincere and confide in ourselves, very clearly stating our mistakes. Always behave ethically. If something is not in accordance with the morality of conscience, then never do it.

People who practice the Tao need to have enough true wisdom. A person with true wisdom never praises himself or slanders others, and never says: "You look at me, I'm the best, the most noble, and the others are all bad, mean things." Those who praise themselves have no way to advance; Although he is alive, he is actually dead; because they went against their moral conscience, despised others, and only cared about themselves. Those are the people that all Buddhas and Bodhisattva never welcome!

If you want to be happily protected by Buddha and Bodhisattva, then what you say and what you do must agree: Words follow actions, actions follow words. (Words follow actions, actions follow words.) Speech and actions must not contradict each other. Don't always boast that I'm this good or that good, but when I do it, it's all corrupt things!

People cultivating the Tao should not have a selfish mind or a mind of self-benefit, but on the contrary, they should benefit others. Don't harm others for your own benefit, or look down on others. Therefore, you must know how to reflect back, review what you have done in the past, what you are currently doing, and then contemplate the future. Always, at any hour, at any minute, do not forget your conscience and morality, then over a long period of time, your good roots will naturally grow and your Bodhi mind will grow strong. Only then can we practice the Bodhisattva Path and benefit sentient beings; So that relationship is solidarity.

We should not lose our Bodhi mind because of fear of demons. Demonic obstacles are challenges and tests. Just like when students first start school, they find the lessons very difficult, but over time, once they have learned a little about the subject, they no longer find it difficult. From elementary school to high school to university, everyone has had the same mentality, so they say: Unexpectedly, the bone is cold for a while, I have apricot flowers and purple scent? (Without a bone-chilling cold, How can the fragrant apricot blossom bloom?)

And: Decades of cold and inhumane questions, One step to become famous in the world! (Ten years of cold weather, no one asked, One day, everyone became famous!)

Like a baccalaureate student who spent ten years studying alone and coldly, with no one paying attention, when he passes the exam and becomes famous, everyone will know. When you practice, don't have false thoughts of wanting to "come out on top," I want people to pay attention to me!

After leaving the home life, if you still seek fame and fortune, that's really worthless. When we leave the home life, we must practice practice in a practical way and cultivate our original blessings and wisdom. To cultivate blessings, you must benefit others; to cultivate wisdom, you must study the scriptures. Often doing beneficial things will give birth to merits and blessings.

Someone asked: "How to benefit others? Is it using money for merit?" That's not true! As long as my mind does not have the heart to kill, do not have the heart to steal, do not have the heart to commit adultery, do not have the heart to lie, and do not drink alcohol, then I have built up my field of blessings. So say: Compassionate speech, Truly expedient, Worthless, Virtuous. (With a compassionate mouth, with a resourceful tongue, Whether you have money or not, you can still do virtuous things.) If your mouth does not curse others, does not say harsh, cruel words, or hurt others, then that is merit. Wherever you are, you must regret your merits and blessings, don't do things that damage your blessings. Wherever we are, we must practice blessings and wisdom. Cultivating blessings and cultivating wisdom cannot be accomplished overnight; It takes a while, but every hour and every minute I have to do it continuously without stopping. Cannot be: One day, the branch is cold, the day is cold. (One day in the sun, ten days in the cold. Hay: One day on, ten days off.)

If we are like that, we will never be able to progress. Therefore, we must recognize the mission, be courageous and diligent, do not retreat or regress. That is the basic thing that people who practice the Way must have!

tieu_de: 24. ALL BEINGS HAVE Buddha Nature
tom_tat: That is a saying from Buddha's mouth. Just because of delusions and attachments, sentient beings cannot realize the wisdom and virtue of the Tathagata. From this saying, it can be inferred that all living beings have Buddha nature; If that's the case then I don't…
noi_dung:
24. ALL BEINGS HAVE Buddha Nature

(Van Buddha Thanh June 20, 1982)

"All sentient beings,

Buddha-nature friends,

The stage of working with Buddha."

That is a saying from Buddha's mouth. Just because of delusions and attachments, sentient beings cannot realize the wisdom and virtue of the Tathagata. From this saying, it can be inferred that all living beings have Buddha nature; In that case, we should not kill, should not steal, should not commit adultery, should not lie, should not drink alcohol; but must maintain the Five Precepts.

When you kill a living being, you kill all Buddhas in the ten directions, because living beings are manifested by the Buddha. Due to a single thought without enlightenment, three very subtle types of ignorance are born (karma appearance, appearance appearance, transformation appearance), so we sink into the sea of suffering and lose the True Path. This principle is very superficial, but those who practice the Tao should contemplate: Visualize that all sentient beings are our parents in the past, are Buddhas in the future, so we must respect them, we must treat sentient beings as if we were treating all Buddhas in three generations! If you think like that, you will naturally stop being contemptuous, disrespectful, or disturbing to living beings.

Living beings are not only tangible, even invisible beings such as ghosts, gods, fairies, and demons are all living beings. Therefore, we must be equally respectful and respectful to them, not to look down on them.

Students of Buddhism need to believe deeply in cause and effect; Don't plant bad causes, otherwise you will receive bad results in the future. If you plant good causes, you will definitely reap good results in the future. Cause and effect cannot be wrong, even if it's as small as a hair! If you kill someone else's father, someone will kill your father; If I kill someone else's brother, someone will kill my brother. So don't use tricks to harm others for your own benefit; Harming others is ultimately harming yourself. Besides: "The virtue of filial piety exists in heaven." Heaven has the virtue of loving life and does not want to harm living beings; So we should never do things that go against cause and effect. You must know that: "The first seven things will turn into eternal hatred. The first seven lives will be difficult to conquer in all lifetimes." Meaning: One stumble, a thousand lifetimes of hatred. Losing a human body is difficult to recover in all lifetimes. It's okay to not believe in anything, but you can't help but believe in the law of cause and effect! Denying that there is no law of cause and effect is extremely dangerous. The Bodhisattvas are only afraid of making mistakes when they sow the cause, but they are not afraid when the fruit is ripe. If the Bodhisattvas accidentally do something wrong without knowing it, then when they receive retribution, they will never have resentment. They neither resent heaven nor blame people. Living beings are afraid of retribution but not afraid of planting causes. When sentient beings plant the cause, it is extremely arbitrary and crazy; But when he receives retribution, he curses heaven, blames earth, and resents people!

tieu_de: 25. SOLID LISTENING TO THE Dharma
tom_tat: Note: On Sunday, June 20, 1982, right at the time of the Dharma Dien celebration, four groups of disciples in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas chanted "Amitabha Buddha" together on the way to the Great Hall, when they discovered a striped green snake lying right at the place...
noi_dung:
25. SOLID LISTENING TO THE Dharma

Note: On Sunday, June 20, 1982, right at the time of the Dharma celebration, the four disciples in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas chanted "Amitabha Buddha" together. On the way back to the Great Hall, I discovered a striped green snake lying right at the front door of the Great Hall, about three or four feet long, very small and elongated in shape. When the crowd saw the snake, they were afraid to enter. At that time, the monk in charge, Master Hang Vo, wanted to throw the snake out. But at that time, the Venerable was also approaching. He smiled and said: "It's not necessary, all living beings have Buddha Nature, the snake comes to get close to the Three Jewels, to listen to the Dharma, don't chase it away!" Strangely enough, this snake is not like other normal snakes, its body slithers out onto the ground, even though hundreds of people walk past it, it is not afraid at all, it is extremely tame and gentle. When the Venerable Master went up to the stage to preach the Dharma, he taught: "Call that snake to come in here and listen to the Dharma." Hearing that, the snake immediately entered. It crawled slowly into the middle of the main hall without frightening the people on either side. Then from the left side of the main hall, it crawled to the right. Then it circled around the Buddha statue, then slowly lay down on the Dharma throne, just like kneeling in front of the Buddha statue, lying still listening to the Dharma. The Venerable just taught him like this:

"All sentient beings

Buddha-nature friends,

Stage of Buddha work.

That is a saying from the mouth of Shakyamuni Buddha. Just because of false thoughts and attachments, sentient beings cannot realize the wisdom and virtue of the Tathagata. From this statement we can infer that all living beings have Buddha nature; In that case, one should not kill, one should not steal, one should not commit adultery, one should not lie, and one should not drink alcohol; but must observe the Five Precepts! Killing is killing all Buddhas in the ten directions, because living beings are manifested by Buddha. Because of a single unenlightened thought, three very subtle types of ignorance are born (karmic appearance, appearance, transformation), sentient beings sink into the sea of ​​suffering, separate and forever lose the true Tao!

Those cultivating the Way, please contemplate: Visualize that all living beings are your parents in the past and Buddhas in the future. Therefore, we must have filial piety towards them, help them escape suffering and attain happiness, cut off life and death, and no longer be bound in the cycle of reincarnation. Because they are future Buddhas, when they have not yet become Buddhas, we must respect them. We must treat sentient beings like we treat all Buddhas in three generations. If you think like that, you will naturally stop being contemptuous, disrespectful, or disturbing sentient beings. Living beings are not just tangible things, even invisible things like ghosts, gods, fairies, and ghosts are all living beings. Therefore, we must be equally respectful and respectful to them, not to look down on them.

Today, the snake you met at Buddha Hall is also a living being. But because it appears as a snake, we feel afraid, see it without realizing it, and are even deceived. This snake only came here to be close to the Three Jewels, to listen to the Dharma, to listen to the Sutras. Otherwise, why would it come here so peacefully, lying prostrate without moving at all on the doorstep?

However, to the naked eye, it is just a small snake; In fact, this snake has the power to transform; can be invisible, can shrink, grow large, and can fly in the clouds and fly back and forth in the air. We cannot know its bravery. If this snake succeeds in cultivating in the future, it will also attain the Way. The Buddha Sutra mentions the Thien Long Bat Bo, this snake belongs to one of those eight families: that is, Ma Hau La Gia (Great python).

Contemplating this snake's cause and effect can be: During the Chau Dynasty, this snake was a Great God, but his mind was very evil and malicious. Because of his plot to usurp the king's throne, he used a dagger soaked in poisoned wine in his sleeve and went to assassinate the king. However, not only did he not usurp the throne, but on the contrary, he also made heaven angry and the people resentful. When that Great Minister was about to die, he had a very angry and poisonous mind, so he died and fell into the body of a snake, and then transformed into a large python.

In the world there are two forces: yin and yang, or good and evil. If you follow the good path and make every effort to cultivate blessings and wisdom, you can become an Immortal, a Saint, a Bodhisattva, or a Buddha. If you follow the evil path and practice, the power will grow bigger and bigger, but it will always do dark things, such as harm, massacre, resentment, revenge, thus accumulating great and dense resentment every day; Those who accumulate deep resentment will later turn into poisonous snakes, poisonous dragons, etc.

Poisonous snakes or poisonous dragons are not things that the human eye can see, but they are abundant in this world. Those poisonous snakes and poisonous dragons are formed by accumulated greed, anger, and ignorance. So wherever they go, there will be disaster. Natural disasters, man-made disasters, non-poems (walking corpses), evil demons (demons that destroy villages), goblins (plants, plants, minerals... absorbing the essence of heaven and earth to form), ghosts (ghosts who have practiced for a long time become demons), or endemic epidemics (incurable diseases) are all caused by these poisonous snakes. As for poisonous dragons and evil spirits, they specialize in releasing toxic gas to confuse people's minds or steal their vitality, making people scared and crazy.

Therefore, currently, all kinds of psychological diseases are circulating, such as schizophrenia, or madness, fear and all kinds of physiological diseases..., all of which are not beyond the scope of causing trouble for these ghosts and demons. Modern psychology and medicine do not deeply understand the causes of those diseases, so they cannot treat them with medicine. Of course, Buddha Dharma has the magic medicine that can completely eliminate all disasters and end all calamities!

Talking about the cause and effect of this poisonous snake: Because you already have an angry mind and cultivate that angry mind, you become pure. Snakes practice magic more and more. Over a long period of time, it penetrates heaven and earth, but only takes pleasure in harming people. There are countless stories similar to this snake in heaven and earth, so I hope they quickly repentance and stop doing cruel things and bringing disaster to the world.

Until the Song Dynasty, this snake became a poisonous dragon. It reigns on a large river that creates storms and storms, killing countless fishing boats, fishermen and tourists crossing the river. For a long time, the people there were extremely afraid and terrified. Fortunately, a very powerful Saint Monk came to the rescue. That man held a staff in his hand and stood on the riverbank loudly reprimanding the poisonous dragon. When the poisonous dragon heard this, he became extremely angry, and then he showed off his full strength, revealing the body of a python thousands of feet long. But the Dharma Master, because he has Vajra Samadhi, is not afraid at all. He used the Summons and the Subjugation method (two methods to subdue ghosts and spirits), spent three days and three nights fighting life and death with it, in the end he conquered the poisonous dragon. Evil cannot prevail! When the evil magic is destroyed, the poisonous dragon has no choice but to surrender. At that time, this Dharma Master preached: 'Everything is suffering, is emptiness, is impermanence, is not-self, and only karma follows the body!' At the same time, He taught him to have compassion, to use magic to help living beings, and not to harm living beings anymore.

After hearing the Dharma, the dragon awakened and had pure eyes. The new Dharma Master ordained him the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts, then told him to go to a certain cave to practice, and not to confuse the people anymore; The poisonous dragon immediately obeyed the teachings. From the Song Dynasty until now, several hundred years of history have passed, and that dragon has become one of the Thien Long Bat Bo, its magical powers have changed immensely."

Once in the Temple of Ten Thousand Buddhas, there was a Bhikkhuni who said: "A few days ago, when passing by Dai Hy Xa Monastery, I saw this snake's tail sticking out, so I took a pick and put it in a wooden box, intending to take it far away and release it so it wouldn't harm anyone. Who would have thought that just by turning around and opening the box, the snake had disappeared. Obviously the snake has no way to escape, but strangely, it really has magical powers."

The Venerable smiled and said: "I've known this snake before! Twenty years ago, when I was at Tu Hung Pagoda on Dai Du Mountain in Hong Kong, he used to come to the pagoda to listen to the sutras. Although it doesn't harm anyone, everyone is afraid of it! Afraid of the snake appearance. One time, someone picked it up and put it in a cage, then took it very far away, I don't know how many miles. When I opened the box to release it, the snake flew away without wings. Nowadays, Buddha's Dharma is spread to the West, this snake does not refuse to fly to America to protect the Dharma.

Finally, the Venerable Master taught as follows: "Students who study Buddha need to deeply believe in cause and effect. If you don't plant evil causes, there will naturally be no evil results. If you plant good causes, you will definitely get good results in the future. Cause and effect are not wrong one bit. If you kill someone else's father, someone will kill your father. If you kill someone else's brother, someone else will kill your brother. Don't think that you can arbitrarily do evil things because doing evil things will be extremely harmful to you. Why? Because heaven has the virtue of loving living beings, it does not want living beings to harm living beings. When we make mistakes with the cause and effect principle: Once a human body is lost, it is difficult to get it back in ten thousand lifetimes. So, it's okay to not believe in anything, but you can't help but believe in cause and effect! If we reject the cause and effect argument, the future will be extremely dangerous. Bodhisattva is afraid of the cause but not the result, so he is very careful when planting the cause. If you unintentionally plant evil, then when you receive the evil retribution, you face the retribution, do not run away, do not resent heaven, and do not blame people. On the contrary, sentient beings are afraid of retribution but not afraid of planting causes. When cultivating the cause, he was very careless in doing crazy things. When he received the retribution, he was extremely afraid, resenting others and blaming heaven: 'Why do I have to suffer like this? Why do I have to suffer such unfair retribution?'

Do you know that if you didn't plant the seeds like that in the past, then why would you reap the results like that now? Today, encountering this fate, Thien Long Bat Bo appeared to preach the Dharma, so I took the opportunity to tell you about the cause and effect.

"Only the first cause before the waterfall,

Thieu willow full table flag."

Meaning: Just make one wrong move, but lose the whole game. A single mistake can be difficult to recover from. Fortunately, this snake has taken refuge in the Three Jewels, and in the future it will still have the opportunity to clear its mind and realize its nature. If you don't believe in this cause and effect, just experiment for yourself; If you believe in cause and effect, then don't doubt this at all!

tieu_de: 26. BE FREE FROM OTHERS
tom_tat: In the world everything changes every day. Humans, all things, time, and space are all
noi_dung:
26. BE FREE FROM OTHERS

(Van Buddha Thanh September 16, 1982)

In the world everything changes every day. Humans, all things, time, and space all change.

This season should not rain, but it rains; It's an unusual climate. Because there are many specific causes and conditions, it changes. Like a volcano erupting because the underground pressure on the land mass above is too great; that is also called variable. People who are erratic are called crazy (neurotic). When the climate is erratic, we call it climate neurosis; Surely something unusual happened. These are not all good phenomena.

During this time, all kinds of disasters and illnesses arise, we need to practice diligently, we have to turn the dark things into good things, we have to turn the calamities into peace. If we don't practice well, when the climate changes, we will change too! When people change psychologically, many problems arise. Therefore, those who study Buddha Dharma, when changes arise, must make special efforts to practice, either reciting the Buddha a lot, or reciting mantras, chanting sutras a lot. When you have strength, you must try to do many good things, because:

Great unjust karma is eliminated.

(If virtue is great, unjust karma can be eliminated.)

In unusual times, we must "depend on unchanging conditions," follow fate without changing. The most important thing is not to get angry, because anger means change, change. If people want to end life and death, they must make efforts. What does effort mean? This means that whatever you do, you must be very sincere. When you encounter disaster, discord, or trouble, don't be moved, don't get upset or angry. That means nurturing the Heavenly nature and Earthly nature within oneself. If you do so, you can patch up the sky and fill the sea, become someone who truly practices the Tao, truly studies Buddha, and seeks the Dharma. Therefore, it is necessary to study clearly and deeply, not to be attached to anything and everything. Whenever we are attached, we are not liberated or free.

"Explore, release, be free." To see means to see through; release means to let go, to throw away. Once you explore, you will understand everything clearly; whenever liberated, liberation occurs; Only with liberation can we become truly free. Without liberation, freedom cannot be achieved. If (yourself) is not there, let (others) be. Forgiveness means being full of false thoughts. If we put it literally, it makes a lot of sense: Forgiveness means that the guest usurps the host's position; The owner is no longer the homeowner. Please pay attention to that point: The owner who cannot manage his house is crazy! There will be no rules in anything!

Releasing means liberation, which means having good karma field precepts, and having left the house of afflictions and ignorance. When you have good karma and receive a certificate, it means liberation. Only with liberation can we be free; If you don't forgive yourself, forgive yourself! If the enemy invaded, he would wipe out all the treasures in the house. Forgiveness means ignorance, delusion, affliction, demons, pagans, ghosts. If we cannot take care of our home, of course someone else will take over. Therefore, you must be very attentive and careful: must be free!

But if you want to be free, you must first see clearly, understand everything clearly:

"May all three hindrances be eliminated, all afflictions will be eliminated, May I attain true wisdom, All vows of sin and hindrances will all be eliminated, I will always practice the Bodhisattva Path." Translated as:

"May I eliminate the three hindrances, be free from all afflictions, May I attain wisdom, be truly clear, May all sins and hindrances be eliminated, Always practice the Bodhisattva Path forever."

That is freedom, self-mastery. If you want to explain deeply, then self-existence means Buddha nature is not present; At that time, the devil reigned inside the house, and he was invaded by the Six Bandits, so even if he wanted to go home, he couldn't. Therefore, from morning to night, I always have thoughts of breaking the precepts. Even though I haven't really broken the precepts, I always have thoughts of breaking the precepts. So what is if that isn't stupidity?

Therefore, if we are not free, we will be invaded by the enemy; Only then can one be the master of one's own house. If self is not present then there is no self-control, it is like being carried by the flow of water, rotating according to the realm. Becoming compatible with people without conforming to the crowd, that is the meaning of not being swayed by the world. Therefore, those who practice diligently do not go anywhere else: right in this body, in this life, in this nature. Whatever you do, you must understand clearly. If so, we will not do foolish things, but will reach a place of unified understanding and action!

tieu_de: 27. EXCELLENT DEMONS
