It is because they cannot do the Four Commandments of Purity: Without lust they cannot do it, without killing they cannot do it! Not stealing, on the surface it can be said that they do not steal, but actually there are many scholars and professors who often steal literature from students or others and then patch it up to make it their own; If you take someone else's property as your own, that's theft! If one day they tell lies to students, then that day they have lied! Of course, not all scholars or professors are like that, but in the ranks of moral people there are always countless harmful liars.

Because they cannot follow the Four Commandments of Purity, they are afraid, and cannot accept the arguments in the Sutra. If they accept the logic of the Sutras, they cannot exist, and of course they will lose their status. But they don't want that, so they go against their conscience and say that the Shurangama Sutra is fake. When they have such thoughts, they have committed a heinous crime:

"Isn't it successful?

Cause and effect bowl,

Arrogant and careless, Chieu is a disaster."

Meaning:

"Denial everything,

Reject the law of cause and effect,

Then you will bring disaster upon yourself."

In the future, they will receive the retribution of falling into the Endless Hell. At that time, it will be too late for them to repent!

tieu_de: FIFTY THINGS OF SACRIFICES IN THE Shurangama Sutra
tom_tat: We are currently studying the Fifty Types of Skandhas, but we are afraid that up to five hundred types of Skandhas will appear here! So don't open the door to welcome them to cause chaos! Although it is said to be a ghost, looking at its appearance...
noi_dung:
FIFTY THINGS OF SACRIFICES IN THE Shurangama Sutra

We are currently studying the Fifty Types of Skandhas, but we are afraid that up to five hundred types of Skandhas will appear here! So don't open the door to welcome them to cause chaos! Even though they are said to be ghosts, looking at their appearance, they come to help you cultivate the Way, to see if your aspirations are solid or not. If you are strong, then even if a thousand ghosts come, you will not change your stance, if a thousand ghosts come, you will not retreat, you will not be afraid of anything! If we don't have what we want, it means:

"There is no place to seek, no worries." (When the heart has no expectations, the mind will no longer worry.)

"Needless" that is, there is nothing to fear. Afraid of what? Just like people who are afraid of demons, think that demons are extremely terrible and ugly. Everyone thinks that dead people turn into ghosts, so they are afraid. But no one is afraid of God. The god Kim Giap is a very powerful man and no one is afraid of him!

Confucius once said: "Respect ghosts and gods, far away." (Respect ghosts and spirits but stay away from them.) However, don't be afraid of demons or gods. We respect them but don't need to be close to them.

Demons are the things that come to challenge those who practice the Way, so don't be frightened or afraid. If you are afraid, even if you don't want to call the ghost back, it will still come. If I'm not afraid, I won't be able to do it even if I want to. That is an extremely important secret: Don't be afraid! When we are not afraid or afraid, we will naturally be righteous. "Chief" then everything can be subdued, because "evil cannot prevail." Ghosts are most afraid of four words: Chief Dai Quang Minh. If we are "righteous and bright" Then the ghosts will obey the rules, they will turn to you and pay homage.

Now let's study the realm of the Fifty Skandhas. Those fifty things are Form, Feeling, Thought, Action, and Consciousness. This is just a brief summary of the essence. To describe them in detail, their realms are countless and indescribable, so Buddha only mentioned fifty to help people understand and observe easily. When we understand the principles of the Fifty Skandhas, we will not be shaken by that realm, which is extremely important.

If you want to not be swayed by your realm, you must first maintain the precepts. Precepts are the basis of all Concentrations; Concentration is the basis of Wisdom; Hue is the basis to become Buddha. If you want to become a Buddha, you must practice Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom. Cultivation that is not compatible with Precepts, Concentration, and Hue means that we seek the dharma outside the mind, that is, we have "turned outward in pursuit"! When we have the power of Precepts, we will attain the power of Concentration; If we have the power of concentration, we will have the power of Wisdom, because they are mutually arising. Precepts give birth to Concentration, Concentration develops Hue, Hue becomes Buddha; Without one, it cannot be achieved.

Therefore, now we must use an objective attitude to research, not a subjective attitude. When there is a subjective attitude, it is easy to be biased. We need to use the Trach Phap Nhan (the eye that knows how to discern the truth) to observe, use the Wisdom of Observation to research, but don't get attached to what we observe. The Wisdom of Wonderful Contemplation is like a mirror, not much different from the Wisdom of Great Perfection. Wisdom of Great Perfection does not waver but can reveal the true appearance of everything; and the Wisdom of Contemplation has the ability to observe everything, allowing you to know everything clearly.

We must use an objective, unbiased attitude to perceive the realm clearly. If you fully understand the realm, you will not be confused by it!

tieu_de: SHURANGAMA GREAT SAMADHI
tom_tat: Why does the Shurangama Mantra have so many good things? Because by reciting the Shurangama Mantra, you can enter Shurangama Great Samadhi. This Great Concentration Shurangama is neither concentration nor non-concentration, but it is never...
noi_dung:
SHURANGAMA GREAT SAMADHI

Why does the Shurangama Mantra have so many good things? Because by reciting the Shurangama Mantra, you can enter Shurangama Great Samadhi. This Great Concentration of Shurangama is neither concentration nor non-concentration, but it is never non-concentration (indeterminate, indeterminate, non-existence, indeterminate time). So say: "Na-age is always in Concentration, Non-existence has no definite time." (Na-gi, that is, dragon, always

In Concentration, there is never no concentration.)

Shurangama Concentration is a very solid concentration, generating immeasurable wisdom, which cannot be destroyed by heavenly demons and pagans.

But what is the purpose of entering Samadhi? For example, going to Disneyland, that place has enough fun things, but also enough horror games, you will see things you've never seen before, hear things you've never heard of. Likewise, when entering Samadhi, we will experience realms we have never seen or heard of before. If in Concentration there is "like immobility, always clear and clear," If we are not shaken by our realms, we can turn all realms around. That is the miracle of entering Shurangama Concentration.

Without Shurangama Concentration, we will turn around depending on the realm. Whatever happens, we will follow that, always guided by the realm. When we have this Shurangama Concentration, we will no longer be swayed by the world. My eyes look at shapes and forms but inside my mind there is no vibration; My ears hear the sound but my heart is not drawn along. When you see something happening and become aware, you will escape the cycle of trouble; But if we encounter things and are confused and not aware, we will fall into samsara.

In Concentration one can generate immeasurable wisdom, so it is said that Concentration gives birth to Hue. If you don't enter Concentration, you can't unlock wisdom, just like if you haven't been to Disneyland, you don't know what's in there. So a lay person invited me to Disneyland, wanting me to see here and there; They thought I had never seen such things before. Actually, the shapes and all the objects are nothing special. From countless lifetimes up to now, we have seen countless things, countless more stories, but we have seen them and then forgotten them. If I remember it clearly, there's no need to review it anymore.

tieu_de: 49. DON'T BE ENJOYED BY SPIRITS
tom_tat: There are many strange things in this world, so many that it is impossible to describe them all. Why are there so many strange incidents? Because human psychology is "curious" and likes strange things
noi_dung:
49. DON'T BE ENJOYED BY SPIRITS

(Van Buddha Thanh April 19, 1983)

There are many strange things in this world, so many that it is impossible to describe them all. Why are there so many strange incidents? Because human psychology is "curious," Likes the weird.

People are curious, so strange things appear in the world. Once those things appear, they fascinate people's minds, making them no longer in control of themselves. Once there is no owner, the family and the nation will also be in chaos. When there is chaos, those ghosts and ghosts show magical powers at will, making people crazy and crazy, running east and west, looking for miracles, miracles, and miracles. Those are all things that have been changed by the realm.

Why are my realms being turned around? It's because of curiosity. This curious mind is inherently greedy. The strange things that happen in this world, if we deeply study their roots, are also created by this greed. If you don't have greed, there's no need to show off strange things, to act especially strange so that people will see you as so spiritual, so good, so unusual. Because people have greedy minds, they are attracted and attracted to those strange things.

Those strange and unusual things are all improper things and belong to demon karma. Righteous deeds are Buddha's karma. So currently, there are many people who have lost right knowledge, right view, right knowledge and correct view. If you preach the true Dharma, they won't listen. No matter how you preach it, they won't accept it. Even if the words enter the left ear, they will go out to the right ear. But if you say strange, special things, they will forever remember and never forget, that proves that people are corrupted by greed!

Why can't they remember the truth? Because they feel there is nothing beneficial for them. In fact, what is true is truly beneficial. Most people in this world accept the fake but refuse to accept the real, accepting robbers as their children. So when I say something honest and truthful, they don't want to listen, but when I say flattering things, they are very happy. It's true: "Chinese language is against the ear, the gums are swollen, medicine is hard on the mouth, the gums are sick." (Honest words are hard to hear but are beneficial for action. Good medicine is bitter but can cure the disease.)

Most people in the world do not want to receive honest words, that is, honest words, nor do they want to drink good medicine, but it is very bitter. If you give them bitter medicine, they will frown and pretend to be uncomfortable, saying: "Oh! This medicine is so difficult to take." But the medicine is so difficult to take that the disease can be cured!

Nowadays people are like that. No one wants to listen to Buddha's stories or Bodhisattva's stories; But if you tell stories about love and ghosts, they like to listen. For example, when people hear stories about boys and girls who don't keep rules and live extremely freely, they enjoy it because they themselves don't want to keep rules. Those are extremely vile, extremely bad ideas.

So, why do some people come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas but can't stay long? It is because they do not have the spirit of sacrifice, do not have the true thought of self-forgetting for the Dharma. If genuine people forget themselves because of the Dharma, even if they chase them away, they will not go; Even if you beat and scold them, they won't run away. They feel that this is indeed where the Dharma lives, they want to approach the Dharma!

We are here studying the Fifty Skandhas, which are extremely useful for this era. If we want to propagate Buddha Dharma, we must have the spirit of great sacrifice, not be greedy for any benefits or conveniences. Whenever someone offers an offering and your eyes shine brightly and your mouth grins, then you are truly worthless!

If you want to save sentient beings, you must first save yourself

tieu_de: EAT MEAT
tom_tat: Living beings are created by the harmony of causes and conditions, and from twelve causes and conditions, they become human beings. From ants to bacteria, all are sentient beings. We don't need to go outside to find living beings, right inside...
noi_dung:
EAT MEAT

Living beings are created by the harmony of causes and conditions, and from twelve causes and conditions, they become human beings. From ants to bacteria, all are sentient beings. We don't need to go outside to find sentient beings, even within our own nature there are countless sentient beings.

Current scientific developments have proven that in the human body there are countless types of bacteria and microorganisms; That means there are countless sentient beings. When people eat meat of any kind of animal, such as pigs, cows or fish, there are countless types of bacteria in it. When humans eat that type of meat, they will naturally have the seeds of those bacteria in their stomachs; The more we eat, the stronger our bond with those bacteria becomes, the deeper our relationship with it, until we are no longer separated or separated!

The more pork you eat, the more likely you are to become a pig; the more beef you eat, the more likely you are to be born as a cow. If I eat more rice, will I be able to turn it into rice? Rice is inanimate, and living beings are sentient. If we eat sentient beings, we can become sentient beings. If we eat non-sentient things (plants), we can help the development of the Dharmakaya and Hue life. If humans do not eat the flesh of any sentient being, it means that they save that sentient being, causing them to cross the sea of suffering and reach the shore of Nirvana. If humans understand this principle, they should not eat living beings.

In the past, someone ate the flesh of living beings, so when they died, they fell down to meet the King of Hell. Whatever flesh he ate from living beings when he was alive, those things are now coming to collect his debt. Meat eaters defend themselves like this: "Even though I eat meat, the crime is not mine but the butcher's!"

Then King Diem La ordered the butcher to come back; The butcher also defended himself saying: "The reason I sell meat is because there are people buying meat. If there are no buyers, then why sell meat?"

The butcher and the meat eater, two people argued with each other, in the end, those two people blamed the butcher.

Diem La Vuong called the butcher in again. This butcher also defended himself saying: "I am indeed a butcher, but because there are people who buy and there are people who eat, I become a butcher. If there were no buyers and no one to eat, I wouldn't be able to do this job!

Therefore, everyone speaks their own reason, the reason they speak is creating karma. As a result, King Yama ruled that the person who ate the meat must compensate for the blood debt. Therefore, if we eat the meat of a living being, we are incurring a grudge against that living being. There is a poem that says:

"Humiliation" From the human side to the two individuals, from the human side to the outside people, living beings return to the flesh and blood of living beings. Meaning:

"In the word "humiliation" There are two people, The one inside eats the one outside, It's the living beings that eat the living beings, Think carefully, it's the one eating the other!"

In the Shurangama Sutra, it is written: "Yang zi is the cause, yang zi is the yang." (A dead goat becomes a human, a dead person becomes a goat.) If a goat can become a human, then a pig can also become a human. If we don't have the Divine Eye Insight, we can't observe that cause and effect, so we think that pigs are pigs and goats are goats. If humans eat a lot of living beings' meat, their original wisdom will be obscured, they will lose their spirituality and become stupid.

Therefore, if you want to save sentient beings, first of all, don't eat meat! If people want to save sentient beings, they must save sentient beings' self-nature, and to save sentient beings, they must separate themselves from form. Without attachments, it is truly saving lives!

LESS ANXIETY, LESS DESIRES

(Van Buddha Thanh June 24, 1983)

Those who practice the Tao are most afraid of suffering, so they say:

"Endless sorrow vows to end."

Getting rid of afflictions is a very urgent matter. If whatever happens, if you don't give rise to afflictions, that means you have the power of concentration. Not having afflictions means not having desires. Desire is the root of afflictions, giving birth to all kinds of ignorance and thus all kinds of diseases.

Not having troubles doesn't mean that because no one bothers you, you don't have troubles; It's that there are people who come to disturb, trouble, hinder, beat, scold, and curse, but we don't create trouble. That's what true concentration is!

52. THE HUMAN EARTH IS UNFORTUNATE, THE RESULT IS SUFFERING

(Van Buddha Thanh July 8, 1983)

The sentence "The cause of the earth is not true, the result is suffering" This is very meaningful; Because whatever you do, do it honestly. If you are not honest and specialize in using tricks and tricks to deceive others, then it is like covering your ears and stealing bells, only fooling yourself!

Regardless of whether a person leaves the home life as a Bhikkhu, a Bhikkhuni, or an Upasaka, an Upasaka, or a Lama, no matter what they do, if they have the mind to deceive others, they will definitely fall into hell in the future. If you are not truthful in life, you will experience devious and troublesome retributions, and you will suffer many hardships in the future.

City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, at every moment, we must pay attention to cause and effect. Don't do things that violate the law of cause and effect. If you know the rules clearly and still try to violate them, you will definitely receive very serious consequences. So you must pay attention, don't do anything wrong with cause and effect!

tieu_de: IF THE BUDDHA CHRISTIAN DOES NOT uphold the precepts, that is the end of Dharma
tom_tat: Today's parallel sentence is: "Buddha followers are weak in maintaining the precepts, which is the end of the Dharma"; That is, if Buddhist followers do not maintain the precepts, then they are dead
noi_dung:
IF THE BUDDHA CHRISTIAN DOES NOT uphold the precepts, that is the end of Dharma

(Van Buddha Thanh June 10, 1983)

Today's parallel sentence is: "Buddha followers are weak in maintaining the precepts, which is the end of the Dharma"; That is, if Buddhist followers do not uphold the precepts, it is the end of the Dharma.

"Buddha Disciple" means monk or person leaving the home life. Buddha preached the Dharma, monks followed the Dharma to practice and then passed it on to others. Sangha must definitely maintain the precepts. If not maintaining the precepts, that is the end of the Dharma; should say: "If Buddhist followers do not maintain the precepts, it is the end of the Dharma."

Whenever we arbitrarily lie, kill, commit adultery, steal, or drink alcohol, we violate the five basic precepts, which is the End of Dharma.

Even if Buddha Dharma exists in this world but we do not uphold the precepts, then we ourselves have created the End of Dharma. The Dharma is transmitted through the Sangha, but it is necessary to take Precepts as the root; Precepts are the foundation to become Buddha. This foundation is like the foundation when building a house. Now that we are building the foundation to build a house of Buddha Dharma, we must definitely take maintaining the precepts as the first step.

You must pay special attention! Do not kill, steal, commit adultery, lie, or drink alcohol. It's not because I don't want to do it, it's because it's in my nature to not do it. It's not because people force us that we don't do it; but because in my heart I am always honest and willing to observe the five basic precepts!

Note: Every week, Venerable Master Hsuan Hua teaches a tureen making class for four groups at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. The content of the class is that the Venerable Master writes a sentence, sometimes 4 words long, 7 words long, or many words, or a poem, and then the audience uses that sentence to make a counter-sentence. The above article is taken from one of those classes teaching how to make parallels. See post #77.

tieu_de: 54. AS A PERSON, YOU NEED TO BE filial to your parents
tom_tat: Humans and animals are different in that humans are wise, know how to be filial, know how to keep customs and order, and know how to appreciate ceremony and righteousness. Not understanding the rules, not being filial to parents, not wholeheartedly loyal to the team...
noi_dung:
54. AS A PERSON, YOU NEED TO BE filial to your parents

(Van Buddha Thanh September 16, 1983)

Humans and animals are different in that humans are wise, know how to be filial, know how to keep customs and order, and know how to appreciate ceremony and righteousness. If we don't understand the rules, don't know how to be filial to our parents, aren't wholeheartedly loyal to our country, and don't know the basic conditions of being human, then what's the difference between us and horses, goats, buffaloes, and cows? So I have to pay attention! Especially students in this era must pay more attention!

Being filial to your parents means knowing how to obey them and making them happy and mentally peaceful; It's not about nurturing your parents, giving them nice clothes to wear, and then thinking that you're filial! Not so!

What is complete filial piety? First, we must know how to listen to our parents' teachings, not oppose or do anything against what they say. You must respectfully listen to your parents' teachings; When responding to your parents, you must be very "beautiful" small, gentle, docile. Whatever parents tell you to do, you must do it right away, don't be lazy or show displeasure or dislike. If you make a mistake and are scolded by your parents, you must happily accept it, not be stubborn or refuse to accept instructions.

In the world, everyone wants their children to become good people, so they teach them strictly. In the Three Character Sutra there is a sentence:

"You are too unruly,

The fall of an unstrict teacher."

Meaning:

"It is the father's fault not to educate his children,

Teaching without being strict is the teacher's fault."

The ancients also taught that: Please show your filial piety! (Under the whip, a filial son can be trained!)

That was an ancient viewpoint, but now there are many places that are out of date; Especially here in America, Westerners have never heard of it. Because in America they say education must be friendly, not beating children, must let children develop freely! In short, if it's too strict, it's not good, but if it's too loose and arbitrary, it's also not good; We have to stay neutral to be reasonable.

The Chinese people pay attention to filial piety. Mr. Tang Sam, a disciple of Confucius, said:

"Parents are not far away, travel must be friends."

Meaning: "When my parents are still around, I shouldn't go far. If I go, there must be a place." The general idea is that as long as the parents are alive, the children should not try to go here and there; If there is something necessary that requires you to go to a far away place, you must let your parents know the exact address so they don't have to worry. Making parents worry is not filial. So the proverb says: Nhi Hanh Thien Ly Mother is assured. (Children travel thousands of miles, mother is worried at home.) That is the image of a mother's care for her children.

55. EXCESSIVE FREEDOM WILL BRING SUFFERING!

In China during the Warring States era and now in the West, people are not much different because of their moral and ethical status.

decadent virtue.

When Confucius composed Poetry and Rites and Music, he prescribed the relationships between king and subject, father and son, husband and wife, brothers, and friends. Discussing those five relationships, he taught that kings and subjects must have Righteousness, fathers and children must have Body, husband and wife must have Distinction, brothers must have Rank, friends must have Faith. He again preached about eight virtues: Filial piety, kindness, courtesy, loyalty, loyalty, integrity, and integrity, and use these eight virtues to maintain order in society.

We should not think that the Western lifestyle of freedom and liberty is good, because in fact, it leads people to do things that are not ethical. Think about it, the behavior of "hippies" cause chaos in the world. Men and women no longer know how to maintain order and are free to be unruly. Their slogan is: "The good will gather, the bad will disperse." (If you like it, it fits, if you don't like it, it dissolves.)

Such thinking makes marriages susceptible to collapse, because they see them as just acting! Most of those plays end tragically, and the person who suffers the most is the girl.

Up to now I have no intention of criticizing, but today there are people who do not maintain social order and destroy good customs, so I feel moved to make a few comments.

Anyone who comes here to practice is not allowed to learn "hippy" habits. liberal, arbitrary, do whatever you like. Such acts truly bring disaster to the country and disaster to the people, so I cannot remain silent. Actions like the above are actions that lead to national destruction and genocide!

56. "HIPPY" WHERE DOES IT COME FROM?

(Van Buddha Thanh September 17, 1983)

The bad behavior of "hippies" From where does it arise? In short, it arises from the laws of the country and the nation! Because according to the current climate, parents cannot strictly discipline their children, nor can teachers punish students for fear of being known to mistreat their children, so they must let their children "develop freely."

You guys try to observe, because "free development" should create a lot of "hippies," homosexuals, and dishonest, delinquent teenagers. They kill people, burn houses, rob, and do all sorts of crazy things. All of these phenomena are due to the concept of "free development" create! Boys and girls are extremely promiscuous, living together naked, singing, dancing, drinking, and smoking drugs, creating a crazy, depraved world; Therefore, the Bronze Pillar and Fire Bed hells are where they will fall and experience suffering after death!

If I didn't truly practice in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas and let the outside world be shaken, I would be extremely heartbroken! Looking at those people brought tears to my eyes. I teach you how to become a wise man, but if you are willing to fall and follow the trend of "free development," then you have indeed been influenced by the ideology of "hippies". This is too deeply infiltrated! I hope that from now on, you will wholeheartedly convert your mistakes and become new people!

tieu_de: 57. SCHOOL IS A HOLY LAND
tom_tat: School is the Holy Land of educating talented people, like a large metallurgical furnace, in which all kinds of iron, gold, and copper are heated, undergoing hundreds of thousands of times of refining to finally become indestructible diamonds. Successful people are...
noi_dung:
57. SCHOOL IS A HOLY LAND

(Van Buddha Thanh September 18, 1983)

School is the Holy Land of educating talented people, like a large metallurgical furnace, in which all kinds of iron, gold, and copper are heated, undergoing hundreds of thousands of times of refining to finally become indestructible diamonds. Those who are successful will serve the country in the future, become a high-paying person, and become a pillar for the country. Therefore, a professor is extremely happy to be able to teach talented people in the world. This is a job that even the gods cannot violate, so we must wholeheartedly strive to undertake this task.

Currently, many schools have degenerated. Not only in universities and high schools, but also in elementary schools, the majority of students smoke and use drugs. Children today are curious, first they learn to smoke, then they learn to steal things. After stealing, you exchange it for money to buy drugs to smoke; and learn the habit of lying and deceiving others. You are citizens of the country, witnessing such a situation and not being sad and miserable is truly heartless!

If you look at the schools outside the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, are you sure you will find a school where students do not smoke, do not use drugs, or sell poisonous marijuana? Never even heard of a school like that! Teachers know but don't care, leaving students to do whatever they want. There are schools that are drug trafficking centers, how dangerous it is!

However, the thing that hurts us the most is that school turns into a place for dates and love between boys and girls, a place where they do lewd things. There are many parents who encourage their daughters to take birth control pills, which is rare in the past; Schools don't care about this, they just know how to collect tuition. In the end, after graduating from school, students have no concept of morality at all, nor do they have any concept of chastity and chastity.

Everyone says: "Freedom! Freedom! Freedom!" That is "freedom" to hell! Such an unkind atmosphere is 100% harmful to people, not even beneficial. If educators do not devise methods for reform, it is difficult to know what the consequences will be.

Therefore, at Van Buddha City, whether it is elementary school, middle school or university, boys and girls study separately. From the time they are young, you must start teaching them about the separation between boys and girls. The incumbent needs to wake up and quickly think of ways to improve the school's decadent atmosphere; by: Vong Duong replenishes labor, due to remaining. Meaning: Even though the goat is gone, if you can fix the barn in time, it's not too late.

tieu_de: 58. WHEN making vows, you need to be sincere
tom_tat: Those who leave the home life to practice Buddhism need to make vows. making vows is to practice diligently. Making vows is to warn yourself, change evil and do good. Cultivating the Way without making vows is like a flower blooming without blooming...
noi_dung:
58. WHEN making vows, you need to be sincere

Those who leave the home life to practice Buddhism need to make vows. making vows is to practice diligently. Making vows is to warn yourself, change evil and do good. Cultivating the Way without making vows is like a flower blooming without bearing fruit, it is impossible.

If you've already made vows, it's best to repeat them every day and say them again, because "we know each other"! We must remember what vow we have made and what we need to do, then the vow we have made will not be an empty promise. I don't lie to myself and lie to others, and at the same time, I don't make vows and then forget about them.

All Buddhas and Bodhisattva in the past were able to attain perfect Enlightenment by truly making vows. All future Buddhas and Bodhisattva will also attain Enlightenment by making vows. Buddha is a Great Wisdom, we are great fools, so we need to learn Buddha's great wisdom. We must take Buddha's mind as our mind, take Buddha's vow as our vow, always learn the four immeasurable minds of Love, Compassion, Joy, and Equanimity, and always practice the virtue of patience with things that are difficult to endure, and do things that are difficult for others to do.

Everything we do must be truthful to be in accordance with the Tao. Therefore, making vows must be sincere and sincere, there can be no deceitful behavior or greed for vanity. That's the point I hope you'll pay attention to. Buddha Amitabha made 48 great vows so he achieved the World of Ultimate Bliss and allowed all sentient beings to leave suffering and gain happiness, to attain birth and escape death. We need to follow Him and all Buddhas and Bodhisattva in the past, and quickly make vows. Only by making vows can one attain Buddhahood!

If you have made a mistake, you must painstakingly correct it, do not cover up or embellish your bad mistakes. We must be very frank in our repentance before the public, otherwise it will only add to our sins. We follow our faulty habits, which means we "overlook the world." Whenever you can correct your mistakes and move towards the good, that is "revealing the world."

making vows is to prevent sin, repentance is to eliminate sin, so say: "Heaven's great sin, One repentance is easily eliminated." (Sins fill the sky, repentance is immediately clean.) Therefore, from now on, I am a new person!

The ancients taught that:

"Tung pre-species,

like carving a jade stone.

The future of races,

like a birthday diamond."

Meaning:

"All kinds of sins from before,

Just like it was dead yesterday.

From here on,

Everything I do is like a new life."

"making vows" and "repentance" Although the two nouns are different, there is no difference at all, just great similarities and minor differences. If you can change bad habits, you have the courage to change, the courage to accept mistakes, the courage to confront reality. Only then can you overcome the challenge and not be shaken by the realm. Don't have an ego that's too deep, don't have an ego that's too heavy. We must understand that we all have a very bright, brilliant, "full, radiant" awareness; All habits and sins in there cannot exist!

tieu_de: STUDYING THE BUDDHA Dharma REQUIRES COURAGE TO CORRECT MISTAKES
tom_tat: You guys! Cultivating the Dao without correcting mistakes is the same as not cultivating the Dao. Studying Buddha Dharma without admitting your sins and then making amends is as good as nothing
noi_dung:
STUDYING THE BUDDHA Dharma REQUIRES COURAGE TO CORRECT MISTAKES

You guys! Cultivating the Dao without correcting mistakes is the same as not cultivating the Dao. Studying Buddha Dharma without admitting your sins and making amends is the same as not studying.

Five years and ten branches of the year,

Nhi knows forty-nine chi phi.

(After practicing for fifty years, I realized my mistakes

during the past forty-nine years.)

A person who recognizes his or her mistakes in the past is a wise person and has a bright future. If you don't know what you did wrong in the past, it's extremely confusing. Whenever they scheme for a false name, they will be fooled by other people. Such people are truly pitiful! We should not send this Buddha Nature into our four great material bodies, then only know how to pursue enjoyment without cultivating the Way.

Why give up the truth to follow the illusion? Why leave the roots to follow the top? It's because we don't know how to reflect, we make mistakes but we don't want to correct them, we don't realize that this self-nature is pure and immaculate, without any impurities. Then, just because we could not grasp our own nature, we had to follow the turbid water, follow the current of pollution, causing our own nature to become cloudy and our original wisdom to be buried; It's even more difficult to clear your mind and see your nature!

We in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas need to wash away this stained and cloudy heart, so that our self-nature is clear and bright. Then use your righteous mind to handle everything, do not use tricks to oppress others. We need to remember that: The Thi Dao stops progressing, the Non-Dao stops receding. (If it is the Way, then move forward. If it is not the Way, then retreat.)

And must know: Trach Thien Nhi survives, Bat Thien Nhi converts. (Choose the good things to keep, change the bad things.) If you do that, you will definitely reach the status of Sage!

tieu_de: TALK TO STUDENTS AT THE SCHOOL OF EDUCATION AND THE SCHOOL OF VIRTUE IMPROVEMENT
tom_tat: Today, young students came to the forum to say their favorite things. Although their words were short, they were very meaningful
noi_dung:
TALK TO STUDENTS AT THE SCHOOL OF EDUCATION AND THE SCHOOL OF VIRTUE IMPROVEMENT

(Van Buddha Thanh September 23, 1983)

Today, young students came to the forum to say their favorite things. Although their words were short, they were very meaningful.

There are children who, although young, already know that lying is a deceitful act. Whenever we deceive others, we will be deceived by others in the future. That is cyclical cause and effect, the principle of retribution.

Some children even recited Confucius's Great Dong, which made me very interested. We hope that Chinese, American, Vietnamese, Cambodian, Laotian children can all recite Dai Dong; and not only can you read in English, but you can also read in your mother tongue.

Today I tell you this news, if the refugees coming here are students, anyone who wants to stay at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to study, I welcome it! Students will receive free scholarships. But children must function independently; Their parents can work outside, while the children can stay in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to study, this is a hard-to-find opportunity!

My time in school was golden because my memory was still good. Therefore, you should memorize any book you read so you don't forget it. When we are in school, we should try our best, not be playful, and not waste time letting time pass. The ancients said: "One block of light and sound, one block of gold, One block of gold and one block of light and sound." (An inch of time is an inch of gold. An inch of gold can hardly buy an inch of time.)

You guys need to remember that! If you don't put effort into studying, your future won't have much hope. Children learn knowledge, learn skills, learn to be human, learn how to become good people. What is learning to be a good person? That means don't get angry, don't argue with friends, don't be greedy, then you're a good student!

Look, everyone in this world has greed, everyone has something they want, and everyone has all kinds of troubles. Those things are all caused by greed. However, the request must also be reasonable and cannot be unrealistic. You can't be unjustly greedy for money, you can't ask for blessings that you have no share in, and you shouldn't have a selfish mind or a mind of self-interest. We must take the Six Principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas as our goal so that in the future, going out to serve society will not only not disturb society but will also make society peaceful.

I hope you will become brilliant and righteous men and women, and will become outstanding and talented people in the future. You should not learn to be rude, have bad manners, be greedy for food but lazy to study, always do messy things, and disrupt society. I also hope you don't learn the "hippy" habit. Don't smoke, drink alcohol, do drugs, or do drugs. You need to make yourself well-rounded in academic knowledge and become a person of excellent moral character.

At Van Buddha City, children are taught English, Chinese, etc. Learning other languages is a very rare opportunity.

Don't miss the opportunity, make an effort to study.

From now on, it will be decided that every Friday afternoon you will come to this forum to practice giving lectures. Don't be afraid, speak loudly, and be "straightforward," That means the logic is solid, the behavior is bold. Because: Mastery creates skill. (Practice well and become skillful.)

If you practice for a long time, you will naturally be able to speak endlessly. Later, you will be able to preach profound morals and become speakers that everyone will definitely welcome. Now is your chance to practice. Every day, if you can proclaim the truth, speak like flowing water, and explain any issue well, then you will quickly become talented people to propagate the Dharma. This is the best time that is very difficult to come across, so don't disappoint me. The ancients said:

"The mountain has its own path, it requires micro-mirror,

Learn the sea without chewing, hard work on the pearl."

(The mountain of books has paths: The way in is diligence.

Sea of learning without shore: Use hardship as a boat.)

If you can use this spirit to study hard, you will definitely make great contributions to the country in the future.

tieu_de: 61. A GENTLEMEN KNOWS HOW TO CREATE FORTUNE
tom_tat: Many things in the world we think are good, but inside there are actually many bad things happening. Right now you think you are extremely happy, but the future can make you miserable. So if you want to avoid…
noi_dung:
61. A GENTLEMEN KNOWS HOW TO CREATE FORTUNE

(Van Buddha Thanh October 1, 1983)

Many things in the world we think are good, but inside there are actually many bad things happening. Right now you think you are extremely happy, but the future can make you miserable. So if you want to avoid suffering, there is nothing better than keeping the Middle Way. The Middle Way means neither too much nor too little, neither sorrow nor pleasure. Trung Dung book says:

"Whoever is lost in joy and anger is in the middle; Phat Nhi is in the middle of the details, and is in harmony." Meaning:

"Happiness, anger, sadness, joy before birth are called Trung; Once emitted and kept at an average level, it is called a Draw.

If you understand this principle, then no matter what you do, you will not be excessive, not confused, and not crazy. We need to know clearly that black is black, white is white, good is good, evil is evil, and discernment is clear so as not to confuse good with evil. The things we encounter in this life are created by the karma of previous lives. Currently, if you want to change your destiny, you need to create many merits. There is a saying:

"A gentleman must learn to create his destiny.

Fate is caused by falling apart,

blessings autism bridge.

Painting, blessings beyond measure,

The only person who tricks himself."

Translated as:

"A gentleman knows how to create his destiny.

The network is made by me,

Blessings I ask for.

Calamity, blessings have no door,

It's just because I brought it on."

Students of Buddhism must clearly understand the law of cause and effect; You cannot arbitrarily create evil karma, cultivate evil people, and you cannot violate cause and effect principles. Therefore, you must be very careful, if you wait until you receive retribution, it will be too late to regret!

tieu_de: 62. DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN Buddha AND MA
tom_tat: Buddha does not have anger, demons certainly have anger; that is wrong
noi_dung:
62. DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN Buddha AND MA

(Van Buddha Thanh October 9, 1983)

Buddha does not have anger, demons certainly have anger; That's where the disagreement lies.

Buddha became Buddha because of the help of demons. Because when He sat under the Bodhi tree, about to attain enlightenment, the devil king became angry, so he sent demon soldiers and witches to threaten and lure Him. But the Buddha was not moved. On the contrary, he used the power of concentration to overcome the magic power, then enlightened him to become Buddha. Therefore, Buddha has no anger or hatred towards ghosts. Demons become demons because they have a strong fighting spirit; So there is a saying:

"Vietnamese victory betrays the heart,

The Dao of Data is infinitely similar,

It is convenient to give birth to the four characteristics of the mind,

How did you attain Samadhi?"

Translated as:

"Fighting is about winning or losing,

Going against the Tao,

Causes the birth of four forms,

How can I attain Samadhi?"

If demon competition is not first-rate, it will give birth to anger, jealousy, and obstacles; Therefore, anyone with such thoughts and actions is a demon and will never be able to become a Buddha. The supernatural powers of demons are no less than those of Buddha; However, the Buddha's magical powers are the right sect, while the demon's magical powers are the wrong sect. Because "evil does not overcome righteousness" So in the end, the demon could not win against the Buddha, so he had to bow down willingly, kowtow and take refuge in the Buddha. But Buddha is compassionate and merciful to sentient beings. He absolutely does not confront demons but only uses morality to inspire and impress them.

Among the Eight Generals of the Path, there is a general called "Hang Ma"; actually called "Sensation Demon" Perhaps it is more correct because Buddha did not use any methods or tricks to oppress, coerce, or subdue demons. If He were to "submit" Demon means that he has the appearance of a self, the appearance of a person, the appearance of living beings, and the appearance of a recipient; If you have these four characteristics, you cannot become a Buddha!

So how did Buddha make Mara surrender? He uses Love, Compassion, Joy, Equanimity, four immeasurable minds. Whenever the Demon King tried to harm Him, He treated Him with compassion and influenced Him with virtue. Buddha knew the principle of "cause and effect"; He knew that the reason why demons came to harass him was because in the past he had created resentment, so now he did not argue, but just calmly accepted the demons coming to harass him.

How can a ghost become a ghost? Because of hatred, resentment, worry, anger, and trouble (6) these five poisons arise! These five poisonous gases help them become demons, so demons always create troubles for others, especially for people cultivating the Way. They see practitioners as a thorn in their eyes, and must find ways to destroy the karma of those leaving the home life. When someone leaves the home life and practices Buddhahood, the ghosts lack a relative, so they try their best to destroy it.

Everyone who leaves the home life must be very careful to avoid falling into the trap of the devil's trick, making it forever difficult to escape. So those who practice meditation must clearly understand their realm, otherwise they will be controlled by demons. "The Fire Pipe Enters the Devil" (The fire pharynx dissipates, demons immediately invade) is extremely dangerous!

Why is it called Buddha? Why is it called a ghost?

Buddha is ethical and reasonable; According to morality, it means matching cause and effect. Demons do not care about morality, do not know about cause and effect. According to cause and effect it is reasonable, not according to cause and effect it is unreasonable. Therefore, the difference between Buddha and ghosts is most obvious at this point. Buddha is full of compassion, but demons are full of anger.

tieu_de: EIGHT BASIC VIRTUES OF BEING HUMAN
tom_tat: Young people, do you know what the basics of being human are? That means there must be eight virtues: Filial piety, kindness, loyalty, faith, courtesy, honesty, integrity, and integrity. Today I will simply explain the meaning of each virtue to…
noi_dung:
EIGHT BASIC VIRTUES OF BEING HUMAN

(Van Buddha Thanh October 12, 1983 - for students)

Young people, do you know what the basics of being human are? That means there must be eight virtues: Filial piety, kindness, loyalty, faith, courtesy, honesty, integrity, and integrity. Today I will simply explain the meaning of each virtue to you:

Hieu: that is, filial piety. Filial piety to parents is the basis of filial duty. Filial piety means repaying the kindness of parents for raising them, and filial piety also means obeying their parents' instructions.

Ðê: that is, respect. Respect those who are older than you. Because you are a younger sibling, you have a duty to respect your older siblings.

Trung: that is, loyal. Being loyal to your country is the responsibility of a citizen. Only by being loyal can you repay the country's gratitude.

Credit: that is, trust. With friends, you must have trust. If you promise something, you must do it. You cannot break trust or break promises.

Ceremony: that is, politeness. To everyone, we must be polite and very humble. Without rituals, we are just animals. Therefore, when you meet your teachers, you must know how to greet them. When you come home and meet your parents, you must know how to be polite.

Meaning: that is, meaning. If you see something meaningful, you have to be brave and do it. When we see someone having an accident, we must do our best to help and solve the problem for them. With friends, we must be moral; When helping someone without any conditions, there is absolutely no intention of scheming, hoping to repay the favor.

Liem: that is, integrity. An honest person, no matter what circumstances they encounter, will not be moved by greed, nor will they want to enjoy comforts. Furthermore, we must have the spirit of "diligence and impartiality," and know how to forget yourself and do things for the common good.

Wholesale: that is, shame. If you encounter something that is not ethical or goes against your conscience, then absolutely do not do it. If humans do not know shame, they are like animals.

Filial piety, kindness, loyalty, trust, politeness, honesty, integrity, and integrity are the eight basic virtues of being human, don't forget them. In the future, when you are born to serve society, you must: Speech must be faithful, actions must be respectful. (Speech must be faithful, behavior must be respectful.)

Whatever you say, be sure to keep it trustworthy and don't lie; Whatever you do, you must be very respectful and honest, and absolutely do not do it for formality.

tieu_de: 64. TAKE HELPING LIFE AS YOUR RESPONSIBILITY
tom_tat: You need to have great will and do great things! Don't think about becoming a big mandarin to make a lot of money because that's just for your own enjoyment, it doesn't contribute anything to the human world. I have to think about how to socialize…
noi_dung:
64. TAKE HELPING LIFE AS YOUR RESPONSIBILITY

You need to have great will and do great things! Don't think about becoming a big mandarin to make a lot of money because that's just for your own enjoyment, it doesn't contribute anything to the human world. We have to think about how to make society happy, how to benefit the nation, how to benefit all humanity. If you think like that, then you are a great man, a heroic hero!

Don't want to study to be a doctor just to get rich, then even if people are not sick, they will still inject drugs indiscriminately to make money. This is against the cause and effect morality, and in the future they will fall into hell. Don't want to be a lawyer because you think this profession makes a lot of money; Then as long as I get paid, even if the person is guilty, I will defend him or her. If we turn the law into a childish farce, how will the losers have any room to complain? Don't be a scientist just because you want to make a lot of money and invent weapons to kill people and kill hundreds of thousands of other people.

Money is something that harms people, makes people kill each other. Relatives turn into nuns, brothers turn into hatred because of fighting over property; I even killed my father for money!

Recently, in Los Angeles, there was a story about a son killing his father as follows: There is a rich man with assets of up to 600 million VND; Perhaps he made his money in a not-so-righteous way. He has two children, both of whom are dishonest young men. Because of money, they plotted to kill their father. You see, is money a good thing?

We must consider money as manure and land. We should not be fooled by money, nor should we lie for money. We must know how to stay calm, work hard, and create happiness for humanity. So there is a sentence: Sacrifice the small self, the child becomes the big self. (Sacrificing the "I" This is a great aspiration, you should encourage each other.

In school, students must first learn how to be human, not learn how to flatter, flatter, or cheat. I don't flatter others, nor do I like others flattering me. We must learn how to have true education, know how to establish words, establish merit, establish virtue, and become an outstanding talented person.

What I tell you today, I hope you remember, don't let it go in one ear and out the other!

tieu_de: 65. IF YOU HAVE A WILL, YOU SHOULD
tom_tat: After leaving the home life, I made vows that I would first translate the Buddha's scriptures into an easy-to-understand form, and then translate them into English. Although I don't know English, I want to find enough methods to translate the classics,...
noi_dung:
65. IF YOU HAVE A WILL, YOU SHOULD

(Van Buddha Thanh October 13, 1983)

After leaving the home life, I made vows that I would first translate the Buddha's scriptures into an easy-to-understand form, and then translate them into English. Even though I don't know English, I want to find enough methods to translate the classics, as much or as little as I can.

After coming to America, my fate matured. In the summer of 1968, I established the Summer Buddha Study Teaching Committee and opened a course to teach the Shurangama Sutra; then took the opportunity to begin translating the classics from Chinese into English. Up to now, many sutras have been translated, but they are not necessarily completely accurate. However, we have tried our best.

Currently, there are many people who understand Buddha's Dharma and many more people who are able to translate, so you should bring the scriptures that were translated in the past and correct them, making them perfect, accurate, and consistent with the Buddha's intention. That is my wish, I hope you will join forces together to complete this merit.

tieu_de: 66. EXCLUSION OF SUPESTIMENTAL CHARACTER
tom_tat: I have the feeling that Chinese Buddhism still has many forms of superstition, full of unreasonable stories, causing people to doubt and not believe in Buddha. Such things certainly require reform; if not fixed...
noi_dung:
66. EXCLUSION OF SUPESTIMENTAL CHARACTER

(Van Buddha Thanh October 15, 1983)

I have the feeling that Chinese Buddhism still has many forms of superstition, full of unreasonable stories, causing people to doubt and not believe in Buddha. Such things certainly require reform; If not radically changed, what will be the future of Buddhism?

For example, people who go to temples to burn incense think that the more they burn, the greater their merit. Actually, that is a misconception. Offering incense to Buddha is a sign of respect; As long as you sincerely light one incense stick, it's enough, there's no need to light many! If the mind is not sincere, no matter how much incense is burned, it will not be effective. Buddha is not someone who likes to smell scents. If Buddha liked scents, he would be the same as ordinary people, there is no difference. Such an atmosphere needs to be corrected, otherwise people will suspect that Buddha is greedy for smelling fragrance. Therefore, I unintentionally polluted His noble virtue, what an extremely sinful thing!

There are ignorant people who come to the temple to pay homage to the Buddha, which is a good thing, but they do not know what bowing to the Buddha means. They only know how to pray to Buddha for promotion, fortune, peace and happiness, then pray for their sons and daughters, pray for fame and fortune, pray for all kinds of things; Those kinds of requests are all manifestations of selfishness and self-interest, without thinking about benefiting people or life at all. If you pray to Buddha and Bodhisattva, it will come true because they do not disappoint sentient beings, but having such a bottomless wish is really wrong!

When I saw such a situation, I felt extremely emotional. We must show those ignorant people how to bow to the Buddha, teach them that they must bow to the Buddha for their faith, for the whole world, for peace, they must bow to the Buddha. Teaching them to pray with a heart of great light, for others, not for themselves, is the true behavior of Buddhists!

There are teachers who lack knowledge and propagate that if you burn votive papers, paper objects, and paper money, you will have great merit, and will give the dead money to spend, and you can bribe the prison guards to reduce the punishment. When people heard what the Teachers said, they immediately bought joss paper and paper money to burn, as much as possible, believing that what the Teachers said was right, because people leaving the home life don't know how to lie! But who knows the secret inside? Those teachers are behind the scenes to take advantage, but who knows? So you must be very wise and considerate, don't let them do anything deceitful or cheat you of money. Such a tactic is truly vile and despicable.

Therefore, I want to reform the blind and superstitious practice of burning votive papers and paper money, so that the Buddhist Church will not be unfairly accused of saying: Buddhism is a religion that promotes and advocates burning votive paper and paper money!

tieu_de: 67. THE BOTTOMLESS GREED OF HUMAN BEING
tom_tat: All humans have greed: greed for wealth, greed for beauty, greed for fame, greed for food, greed for sleep. Greed is bottomless, doesn't know how to stop
noi_dung:
67. THE BOTTOMLESS GREED OF HUMAN BEING

(Van Buddha Thanh October 16, 1983)

All humans have greed: greed for wealth, greed for beauty, greed for fame, greed for food, greed for sleep. Greed is bottomless, doesn't know how to stop.

When people see beauty, beautiful appearance, hear sacred sounds, taste delicious flavors, they are naturally infatuated, and will certainly find every way to capture it. For the sake of temporary enjoyment, people use all sorts of dishonest means to gain it, even though they will regret it for the rest of their lives; What a pity! The ancients said:

"Consistence is always happy,

Patience and self-peace."

Meaning:

"If you know enough, you will be happy,

If you know how to endure, you will be at peace."

How true!

Students! When you study, you must study hard; when you have free time, you must play as much as possible; You can't work without playing, you can't play without working. We must develop in a balanced way to benefit our body and mind; Therefore, the Buddha taught:

"Immortal Emptiness,

Existing two boundaries, showing the Middle Way."

Meaning:

"Do not deviate to either side

Yes and No, is the Middle Way."

We must know how to keep the principle of Trung Dung, not too much, not too little, always just enough. While studying, don't think:

-Why do I have to study?

-A! To make money.

-Why do we have to make money?

-To enjoy, to satisfy material enjoyment.

Thinking like that means that we have left the roots to chase the tops, abandoned the near to chase the far away, and forgotten the basic things of being human, not knowing what it means to be filial to parents, what it is to be respectful to teachers, what it means to be virtuous, what it means to be a good person. Those are the basic things of being human that we completely forgot!

Therefore, the cause of the world's collapse is people's bottomless greed! If everyone did not fight, was not greedy, did not seek, was not selfish, did not seek personal gain, and did not lie, there would be no more suffering in the world!

Students! In the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, these Six Principles are the standard for us to learn how to behave. If we diligently practice those Six Principles, we will become a person different from the worldly person. I do not compete for fame or gain; If so, all afflictions and sufferings will disappear.

You must accept the responsibility to change bad customs and habits, and turn the current broken world into a good world. How to modify? That means we must use Humanity, Righteousness, Respect, Wisdom, and Faith; We must use these five virtues to transform and create a new world. That's called "peaceful heaven and earth", making the world so peaceful!

tieu_de: 68. THE THREE TOXIC THINGS THAT DAMAGE HUMANS THE SEVERELY
tom_tat: If people are greedy, they will never be happy. If you don't be greedy, you will be happy, so you need to "just be greedy," that is, stop being greedy
noi_dung:
68. THE THREE TOXIC THINGS THAT DAMAGE HUMANS THE SEVERELY

If people are greedy, they will never be happy. If you are not greedy, you will be happy, so you need to "just be greedy," that is, stop being greedy:

"Greed in the mind is like nothingness, Filling the mind is difficult, Anger arises. The five desires divide the world and cause confusion, Unconsciously, the Dharma weapon is ice."Translated as:

"Greed is like a bottomless pit,

If you cannot satisfy it, anger will arise.

Five burning desires, crazy thoughts,

Ignoring and not knowing, the Dharma weapon disappears."

Due to greed, there are many relatives who have ruined their reputations, and many people have caused the country to lose their homes. It is true that greed is something that harms people, we cannot help but be careful and hesitant.

When anger arises, we must turn it into nothing, because the fire of anger can destroy all merits. Therefore, those who practice the Way must first learn the method of Patience and Humility Paramita; If you practice until your practice is mature, you can turn anger into compassion. Anger is like water that has turned into ice, and to practice is to turn ice into water, because water can benefit all things.

When delusion arises, we need to eliminate it so that wisdom can appear. Why do I have so many delusions? It's because we are so stupid, and the root of stupidity is ignorance. Due to the impact of ignorance, we give rise to craving thoughts, giving birth to full of delusions. When reason cannot control emotions, we do crazy things; That is extremely dangerous, making it easy for us to lose our karma. Therefore, we must eliminate false thoughts and ignorance will naturally disappear.

In short, when the three poisons of Greed, Hatred, and Stupidity are completely eliminated, then our body and mind will be pure and free from afflictions. When all troubles are gone, you will reach a peaceful state. At that time, there is no worry, no worry, no trouble, no hindrance; Truly extremely free-spirited! Therefore, the meaning is very profound. I hope you will pay attention to studying it thoroughly and you will benefit greatly.

tieu_de: IN THE ORCHIDENT GARDEN, DO YOU KNOW THAT ORCHIDS ARE FRAGRANT
tom_tat: We stay in this ashram every day, studying the Dharma, practicing the Dharma, and being embalmed by incense smoke every day. Gradually, the Dharma and ourselves come together to become
noi_dung:
IN THE ORCHIDENT GARDEN, DO YOU KNOW THAT ORCHIDS ARE FRAGRANT

(Van Buddha Thanh October 16, 1983)

We stay in this ashram every day, studying the Dharma, practicing the Dharma, and being embalmed by incense smoke every day. Gradually, the Dharma and ourselves become one!

Buddha Dharma has five types of incense called the Five Elements of Precepts: About Huong, Dinh Huong, Hue Huong, liberation Huong, liberation Tri Kien Huong. If you marinate these five incense for a long time, you will naturally become enlightened. Newcomers feel that everything at the temple is not good; Fragrance is fragrance, and I am me, it has nothing to do with it. But if you stay here for a long time and are often scented with the scent, you will naturally blend with the scent and form one body; That's why the ancients said:

"Evil and good people live,

Like entering the orchid branch,

Nine children have no words or fragrance.

Evil evil resides,

Like entering the limbs of abalone,

The nine children are unspeakably rude."

Meaning:

"Stay with good people,

It's like entering an orchid garden,

If I stay in U for a long time, I will no longer know the fragrance.

Stay with bad people,

It's like going to the fish market,

After a while, I don't know the fishy smell anymore."

Why is that? Because the person and the external environment have become one!

People with good roots who are embalmed with incense can suddenly achieve great enlightenment, also called enlightenment. What good is enlightenment? That means we understand everything thoroughly, no longer have confusion, and then break through ignorance, allowing wisdom to appear. Ignorance is like a black barrel, you can't see anything. Once enlightened, light appears, breaks through that darkness, and we see everything clearly.

70. WHAT IS THE TWELVE PARTS OF THE Tripitaka?

(Van Buddha Thanh October 17, 1983)

Tripitaka means Sutra Pitaka, Vinaya Pitaka and Abhidharma Pitaka. The Sutra Pitaka talks about the learning of Concentration, the Vinaya Pitaka talks about the learning of Precepts, and the Abhidharma Pitaka talks about the learning of Hue.

After Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha entered Nirvana, the Venerable Ma Ha Kasyapa led 500 people to attain Arhat at Seven Leaves Cave to compile the Tripitaka. At that time, Venerable Ananda recorded the Dharma that the Buddha taught while still alive and made it into the Sutra Pitaka; The Venerable Upasaka Ly brought the precepts that the Buddha taught and rearranged them into the Vinaya Pitaka; Venerable Mahakasyapa took the thoughts of his disciples who studied the Sutras and studied the Law and compiled them into the Abhidharma Pitaka.

The twelve sets, i.e. 12 topics distinguishing the text and style of the Sutra, are summarized in the following verse:

Truong Hang, Duc Trung Tinh Tinh Co Khoi, For example, cause and effect, data self-talk, duty, birth, the monk, Phuong Quang, Treatise on Tho Ky.

Truong Hang: Sutras of this type are written in prose line by line.

Duplicate: That is, the meaning in prose is expressed in verse to repeat the main idea.

Ms. Khoi: are verses and chants written independently, having nothing to do with the ideas before and after the Sutra.

Example: is to use an example to explain the meaning of the sutra text.

Nhan Duyen: is the part that reports the causes and conditions related to what happens.

Narration: Usually, when someone requests the Dharma, the Buddha preaches the Dharma; Only the Amitabha Sutra had no one requesting it, but the Buddha preached it himself.

Born: is the part where the Buddha tells about his past experiences when he propagated the Dharma to benefit living beings.

Duties: is the part that recounts the things that Bodhisattva and Arhat did

did it while practicing.

Venerable Zeng Huu: is about miraculous transformations that have never been heard before.

Phuong Quang: is the main and generous part of the scriptures

to the realm of peace and harmony without hindrance.

Discussion: is a report on the disciples' study of the Sutras and Vinaya, or a record of the discussion between the Buddha and his disciples.

Tho Ky: is the part that refers to the Buddha's predictions for the Bodhisattva, such as when they will become Buddha, when they will be born in Pure Land, in which Pure Land they will become Buddha, or predictions, etc.

I introduce the twelve Tripitakas in such a simple way so that you can have an initial impression. Wishing you all to deeply understand the Sutra Pitaka, and develop wisdom as vast as the ocean.

tieu_de: The Sixth Patriarch was in Hiding Place with a Group of Hunters.
tom_tat: When the Sixth Patriarch Huineng was at Dong Son Pagoda in Hoang Mai, he received the initiation from the Fifth Patriarch Hoang Nhan. The Fifth Patriarch taught him to quickly return to Guangdong and hide himself, become a hermit, not compete with the world, and not reveal his identity...
noi_dung:
The Sixth Patriarch was in Hiding Place with a Group of Hunters.

When the Sixth Patriarch Huineng was at Dong Son Pagoda in Hoang Mai, he received the initiation from the Fifth Patriarch Hoang Nhan. The Fifth Patriarch taught him to quickly return to Guangdong and hide himself, to be a hermit, not to compete with the world, not to reveal his identity, and not to seek fame. Because of that fate, the Sixth Patriarch escaped; However, it was not the Fifth Patriarch who taught him to hide in the cave and not let anyone see him. That is the point that we need to distinguish clearly.

Where is the Sixth Patriarch hiding? He stayed there wherever he met, hiding in a group of hunters and staying with them for more than fifteen years. He hid his identity to practice and mingled with the secular world to cultivate the Way. No one could guess that he was the one who attained the Dharma. At that time, the Sixth Patriarch had not yet left the home life, he was just a lay person.

We are cultivators of the Tao, no matter what situation we encounter, we must "take away the light of regret." It means covering up one's practice and not revealing the truth. Only then can one practice. On the contrary, it is very difficult to practice.

You cannot go everywhere advertising that you have such and such practice, that you have practiced meditation for so many years and so and so. Running from place to place proclaiming one's practice is not the behavior of someone leaving the home life, of someone cultivating the Tao!

You must be very sincere when practicing, not advertising yourself, wanting people to raise their heads and look at you with respect; because that is extremely wrong, disqualifying the person leaving the home life! There is a proverb that says:

"Natural musk incense,

Ha Nhu Dai Phong Duong?"

Meaning:

"With musk, it naturally smells good,

Why wait for a strong wind to blow to smell good?

tieu_de: 72. DESTROYING THE VIEW OF HUMAN EGO, DIVIDED BUDDHA TEACHING
tom_tat: Now I feel like many of the things I did in the past were very wrong. What are mistakes? Buddhism promotes "no self" but I often have a "self"; Because there is a "self", we do not know others...
noi_dung:
72. DESTROYING THE VIEW OF HUMAN EGO, DIVIDED BUDDHA TEACHING

Now I feel like many of the things I did in the past were very wrong. What are mistakes? Buddhism promotes "selflessness" but I often have a "self"; because there is a "self" so don't know other people. Basically, "forget yourself, forget others" that's right; However, I "miss myself, forget others"! Because we forget about others, we don't know how much work they have done for Buddhism; That was a mistake that made me feel extremely guilty.

Currently, Western Buddhism is beginning to develop, you must make concerted efforts, unite and agree to support Buddhism, and unite to promote Buddhism. We should not refute each other, divide sects, defend our temple, criticize other temples; There should be no division between skin color and nationality. Regardless of whether they are Mahayana or Hinayana, everyone should unite together and truly practice so that Buddhism can develop more and more!

You must bring the "self" put it aside, consider others and yourself as one, and set an example for others, only then will the future of Buddhism become bright. Just take each step like that to touch others; Don't use force to intimidate, but use morality to make people admire you. Do not act arrogantly or threaten people; You should also not be arrogant, arrogant, and think that you are better than everyone else. Because doing so means still having ego views, ego attachments, arrogance, and ego appearances; If those things are not eliminated, they will become obstacles on the path of the Path, causing the Buddha's teachings to gradually weaken and we will sin against Buddha.

You must take the revival of Buddhism as your responsibility, not afraid of hardships, not afraid of difficulties. For the sake of Buddhism, make efforts and voluntarily devote yourself to Buddhism without any intention of scheming or calculating. If everyone can do that, then how can Buddhism not have a revival? We must preserve the principle: "Someone else's fault is your own fault." We must have such thoughts to not give birth to discrimination and division, and to not have a distorted view. I often say:

"True acceptance of self-denial,

Discourse on other people's non-existence.

Tha phi means self phi,

Same name as Great Compassion."

Meaning:

"Admit that you're wrong,

Don't talk about other people's faults.

Other people's faults are our faults,

The new unity of Great Compassion."

If we can do so, there will definitely be peace everywhere, with absolutely no mind for conflict; by:

"Things are past,

Spleen qi turns into a willow.

True energy is lifeless,

The title is priceless.

Weak and resentful people,

The great potential.

Affliction is eternal and unborn,

Harsh na ly claw?

Often the scoundrel is in opposition,

Autistic bitter taste willow!"

Translated as:

"Everything goes smoothly,

Being hot makes it difficult to cool down.

If you really don't get angry,

That's it, priceless.

If you don't resent people,

Everything will go smoothly.

Forever without worries,

Why do you chase unjustly?

Just keep looking at people's mistakes,

My suffering still hasn't subsided!"

In the past, I only saw other people's mistakes, so I was very miserable. Now I consider everyone to be right, so I feel very comfortable. The phrase "the beginning of meditation" mine is: "Everything is O.K.!" Thus, everything will be beneficial, lucky and smooth.

tieu_de: 73. PRACTICES NEED TO PASS THE TESTS
tom_tat: Those who study the Buddha Dharma must definitely eliminate the mind of selfishness and self-interest, not let their concentration be damaged, but must change to the mind of "forgetting themselves for the Dharma." Just to hear the Buddha Dharma, even if they have to give their body and life...
noi_dung:
73. PRACTICES NEED TO PASS THE TESTS

(Van Buddha Thanh October 25, 1983)

Those who study the Buddha Dharma must definitely eliminate the mind of selfishness and self-interest, not let their concentration be damaged, but must change to the mind of "forgetting oneself because of the Dharma." As long as you hear the Buddha Dharma, even if you have to give your body and life, you will not have the slightest regret or remorse. You must know that:

"The highest path,

The highest level of magic.

The highest religion,

The devil is at the top."

Meaning:

"The Tao is one span tall,

Mac high level.

The religion is at a high level,

Ghost on my head."

The more you want to practice, the more tests you will have to test to see if you can realize it or not. People who want to practice the Way must first eliminate greed, have no anger, and have no predestined relationships.

Not using predestined relationships generally means not using tricks to get money or things from others. You must definitely eliminate greed, anger, and ignorance; Because if these three poisons remain, all kinds of troubles will arise!

Each person does not know their own karma, but when they begin to truly practice, they often create all kinds of karma; that's because:

"If you learn well, you will be punished harshly,

We need to become a Buddha, a fairy and a demon."

Meaning:

"If you want to study well, you will find hardship. If you want to become a Buddha, you will first meet the devil."

Currently (1979), a "Three Steps One Worship" Master Heng Trieu just left the home life, setting out to "prostrate every three steps." As soon as he learned what it means to practice the Tao with effort and return to his duty, suddenly the Master's mother became ill and had to go to the hospital for surgery. The surgery is not difficult, but it causes all kinds of delusions to arise in the Master's mind, so bowing to the Buddha becomes bowing to delusions! What a formidable challenge. If the mind is not steady, it will be shaken by the realm. However, although inside the mind is moving, outside the body is still bowing; and I used my strong will to overcome those delusions.

Think about it, practicing is not an easy thing! Master Heng Trieu feels that in other realms, he can keep his mind unshaken, but in this realm (mother's illness), he is somewhat unable to keep his mind steady. Even though he couldn't bear it, he still continued his journey, "One bow in three steps," appears not to be swayed by the realm.

Religious practitioners need to pay attention! It is impossible to start false thoughts! False thoughts are the rock that binds a practitioner's feet; If there are any false thoughts, there will naturally be that realm to test. So I often say:

"The test is absolutely necessary,

My audience is a magician.

Facing unconscious weakness,

Practice again and again."

Meaning:

"Everything is a challenge,

Let's see how you handle it.

Faced without knowing,

Had to start over from the beginning."

Just like a boy cannot let go of his wife, a girl cannot let go of her husband, children cannot let go of their parents, and parents cannot let go of their children; These are all situations to test yourself. It's also because of that inability to let go that we can't practice. When the realm comes, it will not be easy for us to overcome this barrier. There is a saying: Cultivating the Dao is like a woman with hundreds of red canes. In the future, it is easy to overcome difficulties. Meaning: Cultivating the Way is like climbing a hundred meter pole. Sliding down is easy but climbing up is difficult.

What do you think about now? If we don't move forward, we will fall back. If you move forward, you will advance easily, but if you move backward, you will easily fall down. Going up is the good path, going down is the evil path; really:

"Nan! Nan! Nan!

Practicing one word is cold and spiritual.

Cultivation arises, longing for sleep,

The tide is no longer comfortable."

Meaning:

"Difficult! Difficult! Difficult!

"Practice" two cold words.

Stay up late, wake up early,

There is no rest day or night!"

Tell me, is it difficult or not difficult?

tieu_de: 74. PRACTICES NEED TO KEEP BODY AND MIND
tom_tat: People leaving the home life to practice Buddhism always need to take care of their body and mind, and cannot arbitrarily indulge in distractions and scandals! Staying in the ashram and practicing for one day without progress means you have regressed, so it is said
noi_dung:
74. PRACTICES NEED TO KEEP BODY AND MIND

People leaving the home life to practice Buddhism always need to take care of their body and mind, and cannot arbitrarily indulge in distractions and scandals! Staying in the ashram and practicing for one day without progress means you have regressed, so it is said:

"A single day can't be changed, a single day can't be created!

Meaning: "A day of mistakes without correction is a day of no merit! People leaving the home life need to strictly observe the four postures of walking, standing, lying down, and sitting:

"Act like wind,

Sit like a general,

Set up like a pine tree,

Crouching like a bow."

Meaning:

"Go like the breeze,

Sitting like a bronze bell,

Stand straight like a pine tree,

Lie down like an extended bow."

When walking, it must be like a breeze blowing so gently that the surface of the water on the river does not stir; Don't go like an extremely fierce whirlwind that makes the sea surface rise like a dune, rising hundreds of meters high. When sitting, you must sit like a bell, very steady; Don't sit like a bell, shaking it from right to left, never stopping. When standing, the head and body must be straight and serious, like a pine tree. Pine trees grow straight, tall, alone, not relying on anything else. When lying down, you must lie in the "auspicious" position. that is, the side of the face is below, just like the bow in the drawn position. People leaving the home life must pay special attention to these four postures.

Practitioners should not just say that, but must be very cautious and gentle. Wherever you go, you must set an example for others. You cannot laugh, joke, talk nonsense, because that means not respecting the rules of the ashram.
